confirmed.title: If the per-side basket/time stop only partly closes, the stop moves to the next layer and averaging resumes (the v6.12 bug again)
confirmed.detail: V7GridExits ignores CloseAll's return value: `CloseAll(magic); continue;` (basket, line 1291) and `CloseAll(magic);` (time stop, line 1299). Nothing records that the side is stopped, so the rest of OnTick runs as usual: ReadGrid, then `TryAddLayer(...)` at lines 554-558, which only checks `layersOK`. On every tick the anchor is read again from live positions. GridTimes takes `firstPx` from whichever surviving position is oldest (lines 1217-1222). EnsureSL then sets every ticket's SL from that anchor, `double sl = BrokerSL(type, firstPx);`, and nothing stops it moving an SL further away (line 1425). If layer 1 closes but a later layer does not, the virtual stop, the broker SL and the NoAddAfterSec/MaxHoldSec clocks all re-anchor to layer 2. If every close fails, layer 1 stays and the stop re-fires each tick, but TryAddLayer can still add a new layer in the same tick (count < maxL, price at least one step below lastPx). The v6.13 header calls exactly this a v6.12 bug, fixed for EmergencyCloseDD with g_haltFlatten. The new v7 stop has no such latch. The same partial-close pattern exists in the v6.13 pre-news close with NEWS_CLOSE_PROFIT (line 492): once the remainder is negative it is never retried, and adds continue unless NewsPauseLayers is on. The Strategy Tester never produces partial close failures, so backtests cannot show this.
confirmed.failure_scenario: $100 account, StopPips=10, spacing 75 pts, 0.01 lots, so the ladder fit allows 2 layers (L1 at 0, L2 at -7.5 pips). Price hits L1-10 in a fast move. CloseAll closes L2 first (highest index), then L1 succeeds, or L2 fails 3 times with REQUOTE/PRICE_OFF/TOO_MANY_REQUESTS. Take the case where L1 is closed and L2 is left. Next tick: firstPx = L2, so the stop becomes L1-17.5. Within 60 s EnsureSL moves L2's broker SL from L1-12 to L1-19.5. TryAddLayer adds L3 at L1-15 because count 1 < g_effMaxLayers 2. Realised loss is about 10+10+2.5 pips against a fitted budget of 10+2.5, about 1.8x MaxBasketRiskPct, and it compounds on deeper ladders. If the terminal's position list lags after the close (the code assumes such lag at lines 750-762), the same-tick add can also open a fresh layer straight after a successful stop.
confirmed.fix: Add a per-side latch `bool g_sideFlat[2];`. In V7GridExits, set g_sideFlat[k]=true on a basket or time hit. At the top of the loop: `if(g_sideFlat[k]){ if(PosCount(magic)==0) g_sideFlat[k]=false; else { CloseAll(magic); continue; } }`. Gate adds: `if(bCount>0 && layersOK && !g_sideFlat[0]) TryAddLayer(...)` (same for SELL), and skip OpenLayer1/EnsureSL for latched sides. Persist the latch in a GlobalVariable. In EnsureSL never loosen an existing SL: BUY `if(cur>0 && sl<cur-g_point) continue;`, SELL `if(cur>0 && sl>cur+g_point) continue;`. Better still, persist each side's L1 anchor price and time when layer 1 fills and use that, not the oldest surviving ticket.
confirmed.reason: The code matches the claim. V7GridExits (1291, 1299) ignores CloseAll's return value and sets no per-side state. GridTimes (1217-1222) re-derives firstPx and oldestMs from the oldest SURVIVING ticket on every tick. So once L1 is closed and L2 is not, StopPrice and BrokerSL re-anchor to L2. EnsureSL (1425-1432) then sets every ticket's SL to the new, looser value, because it only checks |SL - target| <= point. MaxHoldSec and NoAddAfterSec restart from L2's open time. TryAddLayer (554-558) is gated only by layersOK, so with count < g_effMaxLayers it averages again. I checked the arithmetic: with StopPips=10 and spacing 7.5 pips, FitLayers gives n=2 by geometry, since k=3 has dist<0. A remnant L2 then has its stop at L1-17.5 and adds L3 at L1-15. Loss is about 22.5 pips x lot against the fitted 12.5. There is a second hole the reviewer did not mention. If every close fails and the next tick bounces back above the stop, `hit` is false, nothing retries, and the grid carries on as if the stop never fired. EmergencyCloseDD has the g_haltFlatten latch for exactly this (header lines 30-32); the v7 stops do not. The pre-news NEWS_CLOSE_PROFIT sub-point is also accurate (line 492: once the remainder's float is below 0 it is never retried), but it dates from v6.13, not v7. The Strategy Tester never fails a close, so no backtest can show any of this.
confirmed.fix_final: 1) Globals: `bool g_sideFlat[2];` (zero-initialised). 2) In V7GridExits, right after magic and type are set: `if(g_sideFlat[k]) { if(PosCount(magic) == 0) { g_sideFlat[k] = false; GlobalVariableDel(GvName(k == 0 ? "flatB" : "flatS")); } else CloseAll(magic); continue; }`. On a basket or time hit, set the latch BEFORE closing, whatever the outcome (this also covers position-list lag): `g_sideFlat[k] = true; GlobalVariableSet(GvName(k == 0 ? "flatB" : "flatS"), 1); CloseAll(magic); continue;`. 3) Gate the latched side everywhere: `if(bCount > 0 && layersOK && !g_sideFlat[0]) TryAddLayer(...BUY...);` and the same for SELL with [1]; `if(bCount == 0 && wantBuy && !g_sideFlat[0] && OpenLayer1(...))`; skip HealTP and EnsureSL for a latched side. 4) OnInit: `g_sideFlat[0] = GlobalVariableCheck(GvName("flatB")) && PosCount(MagicBuy) > 0;` and the same for [1] with "flatS"/MagicSell. 5) EnsureSL must never loosen an SL. After the existing equality check add: `double cur = PositionGetDouble(POSITION_SL); if(cur > 0 && ((type == ORDER_TYPE_BUY && sl < cur - g_point) || (type == ORDER_TYPE_SELL && sl > cur + g_point))) continue;`. 6) Recommended: when L1 fills, persist the side's anchor (fill price and time_msc) in GVs, use it in V7GridExits, EnsureSL and TryAddLayer in place of GridTimes' oldest-survivor values while the side has positions, and clear it when the side is flat.

confirmed.title: No hedging-account check: on a netting account the grids net out, and the stop and layer count stop working
confirmed.detail: OnInit validates magics, lots and v7 inputs but never checks ACCOUNT_MARGIN_MODE (grep finds no MARGIN_MODE anywhere). On a netting account the BUY and SELL magics share one position per symbol. ReadGrid then always returns count=1, and lastPx/firstPx = POSITION_PRICE_OPEN is the averaged price. So `if(count >= maxL) return;` never fires. Each add moves the average down by step/(n+1), so the next add trigger and the virtual stop `StopPrice(type, firstPx)` both follow price down. Each add's `req.sl` also replaces the netted position's SL with a lower one. In SYMMETRIC mode the SELL L1 just closes the BUY L1 on every EntryTF bar.
confirmed.failure_scenario: An account opened as netting, which some brokers use by default for some account types, with STRETCH mode and StopPips=10, fit=2. A BUY signal opens 0.01 lot. As price falls, an add fires whenever ask <= average-7.5 pips. Because the average keeps falling, the stop (average-10) is never reached while price falls steadily. Lots grow until margin returns NO_MONEY or MaxTotalLots (default 8.0) is hit. In SYMMETRIC mode with EntryTF=M1 the EA pays a full round trip every minute.
confirmed.fix: In OnInit: `if((ENUM_ACCOUNT_MARGIN_MODE)AccountInfoInteger(ACCOUNT_MARGIN_MODE) != ACCOUNT_MARGIN_MODE_RETAIL_HEDGING) { Print("FATAL: hedging account required"); return INIT_FAILED; }`
confirmed.reason: OnInit has no ACCOUNT_MARGIN_MODE check (grep finds no MARGIN_MODE, HEDGING or NETTING anywhere). The whole design needs two independent position sets per symbol. On a netting account there is one position per symbol: ReadGrid returns count<=1, and POSITION_PRICE_OPEN is the volume-weighted average. So `count >= maxL` never stops adds, and lastPx and firstPx both follow the average down, which drags the add trigger and the virtual stop with price. In SYMMETRIC mode the SELL L1 sent in the same tick simply closes the BUY L1, so the EA pays a full round trip on every EntryTF bar. This has been missing since v6. It is a missing guard, not a logic bug in the hedging path, and it only matters if the EA is ever attached to a netting account. Even so, a one-line fatal check is warranted.
confirmed.fix_final: In OnInit, after the magic check: `if((ENUM_ACCOUNT_MARGIN_MODE)AccountInfoInteger(ACCOUNT_MARGIN_MODE) != ACCOUNT_MARGIN_MODE_RETAIL_HEDGING) { Print("FATAL: a hedging account is required (two magic-isolated grids). Aborting."); return INIT_FAILED; }`

confirmed.title: Daily loss stop is lost on any re-init, and the day restarts from the already-reduced balance
confirmed.detail: OnInit unconditionally runs `g_dayStart = 0; g_dayHalt  = false;`. On the next tick V7AccountGuards sees `day != g_dayStart` and sets `g_dayBal = AccountInfoDouble(ACCOUNT_BALANCE); g_dayHalt = false;` (lines 1312-1317). That is the balance at re-init, not at server midnight. OnInit runs on terminal or VPS restart, on any input edit, and on a chart symbol or timeframe change, which by the MQL5 docs calls OnDeinit/OnInit without unloading the EA. Neither g_dayHalt nor g_dayBal is persisted, unlike the kill latch. The input promises 'Flatten + stop for the day'. A second smaller gap: at server midnight g_dayHalt is cleared even if a flatten is still failing (`if(g_dayHalt && nOpen > 0)`), so leftover positions go back to normal management.
confirmed.failure_scenario: DailyLossPct=6 on $100. By 14:00 losses reach -6%, so the EA flattens and halts with balance $94. At 15:00 the user switches the chart from M15 to M5, or Windows Update restarts the VPS. OnInit sets g_dayHalt=false, the first tick sets g_dayBal=94, and trading resumes with a fresh 6% (about $5.64). The day can end near -11.6%, or worse after several restarts.
confirmed.fix: Persist the halt: `GlobalVariableSet(GvName("dayhalt"), (double)g_dayStart)` when it fires, and on day detection restore `g_dayHalt = (GlobalVariableGet(GvName("dayhalt")) == (double)day)`. Compute g_dayBal from history rather than current balance: HistorySelect(day, TimeCurrent()+60), then dayBal = balance minus the sum of DEAL_PROFIT+DEAL_SWAP+DEAL_COMMISSION+DEAL_FEE of all deals since `day`. Do not clear g_dayHalt at rollover while nOpen>0.
confirmed.reason: OnInit sets `g_dayStart = 0; g_dayHalt = false;` unconditionally (306-307). On the next tick `day != g_dayStart` is true, so g_dayBal becomes the CURRENT balance and g_dayHalt is cleared (1312-1317). Nothing is saved to a GV. On a chart symbol or timeframe change the runtime keeps global variables, but OnInit clears these two itself, so the halt is lost on every reinit reason, not just a terminal or VPS restart. The rollover sub-claim is also correct: at server midnight g_dayHalt is cleared even if positions from a failing flatten are still open, and they go back to normal management (adds and TP).
confirmed.fix_final: Move `int nOpen = ...` above the day block. Then in V7AccountGuards: `if(day != g_dayStart) { if(GlobalVariableCheck(GvName("dayStart")) && (datetime)(long)GlobalVariableGet(GvName("dayStart")) == day) { g_dayBal = GlobalVariableGet(GvName("dayBal")); g_dayHalt = GlobalVariableGet(GvName("dayHalt")) > 0.5; } else { g_dayBal = AccountInfoDouble(ACCOUNT_BALANCE); if(nOpen == 0) g_dayHalt = false; GlobalVariableSet(GvName("dayStart"), (double)(long)day); GlobalVariableSet(GvName("dayBal"), g_dayBal); GlobalVariableSet(GvName("dayHalt"), g_dayHalt ? 1 : 0); } g_dayStart = day; }`. Add `datetime g_dayHaltDay;` and release a carried-over halt once flat: `if(g_dayHalt && nOpen == 0 && g_dayHaltDay != g_dayStart) g_dayHalt = false;`. When the limit fires: `g_dayHalt = true; g_dayHaltDay = g_dayStart; GlobalVariableSet(GvName("dayHalt"), 1); GlobalVariablesFlush();`. Optionally, so that withdrawals are not counted as losses, rebuild the baseline as balance minus today's DEAL_TYPE_BUY/SELL deal P/L (profit+swap+commission+fee), leaving out DEAL_TYPE_BALANCE/CREDIT.

confirmed.title: Equity peak is tracked and saved even with PeakKillPct=0, and withdrawals count as losses, so enabling the kill or withdrawing can force an immediate flatten
confirmed.detail: V7AccountGuards runs `if(eq > g_eqPeak) g_eqPeak = eq;` on every tick regardless of PeakKillPct. OnDeinit always writes `GlobalVariableSet(GvName("eqpeak"), g_eqPeak);`, and OnInit restores `MathMax(g_eqPeak, GlobalVariableGet(...))`. The peak includes transient floating profit. GridEquity is balance plus EA float, so a withdrawal (or another EA's loss) lowers eq exactly as a trading loss would. The same applies to `eq - g_dayBal` in the daily check.
confirmed.failure_scenario: The EA runs for weeks with PeakKillPct=0 and GridEquity peaks at $130 (balance $120 plus a floating grid). The account later drifts to $100 and the user enables PeakKillPct=20. On the first tick, 100 <= 130*0.8=104, so KILL fires, open grids are flattened at a loss, and the latch persists. Similarly, withdrawing $25 from a $120 account at peak trips a 20% kill, and a $7 withdrawal trips DailyLossPct=6.
confirmed.fix: Track and save eqpeak only while PeakKillPct>0. Store the PeakKillPct that was active, and reset the peak to current equity when the feature is first enabled. Adjust the peak and the day balance for DEAL_TYPE_BALANCE deals (deposits and withdrawals) found in history.
confirmed.reason: Line 1318 updates g_eqPeak on every tick whatever PeakKillPct is. OnDeinit always saves it (379), and OnInit restores the MAX (298-299). Switching PeakKillPct on later therefore measures against a peak recorded while the feature was off, which can include old floating profit. That can kill immediately on the first tick. GridEquity is ACCOUNT_BALANCE plus EA float, so a withdrawal, or another EA's realised loss on the same account, lowers it exactly as a trading loss would. That applies to both the peak kill and `eq - g_dayBal`. A 20% withdrawal therefore flattens the grids at a loss and latches the EA. Measuring drawdown from the peak is reasonable in itself; the defects are the tracking while the feature is off and the balance-operation contamination.
confirmed.fix_final: Wrap the peak update and its save in `if(PeakKillPct > 0)`. Save the active PeakKillPct in GV "killpct"; in OnInit, if that GV is missing or differs, reset g_eqPeak = GridEquity(). Each tick (throttled), scan HistorySelect(g_lastBalScan, TimeCurrent()) for DEAL_TYPE_BALANCE/DEAL_TYPE_CREDIT deals and shift both g_eqPeak and g_dayBal by each deal's DEAL_PROFIT, so deposits and withdrawals do not count as P/L. Then advance g_lastBalScan.

confirmed.title: Kill latch and equity peak can be lost on a crash; leaving ResetKillLatch=true turns persistence off
confirmed.detail: `GlobalVariableSet(GvName("kill"), 1);` is never followed by GlobalVariablesFlush(). The MQL5 docs say global variables are written to disk at terminal shutdown and can be lost on an abrupt failure. eqpeak is written only in OnDeinit (line 379), which does not run on a crash. Separately, `ResetKillLatch` deletes both GVs on every init while it is true, and users set it to true to clear a latch.
confirmed.failure_scenario: Equity rises from 100 to 125 with no clean deinit, so the saved peak is still 100. The kill fires at 100 (-20%) and positions are flattened. The VPS then hard-reboots before a flush. On restart g_kill=false and g_eqPeak=max(100, saved 100)=100, so trading resumes, and the next kill is at $80 rather than the latched stop. A user who left ResetKillLatch=true loses the latch on every restart.
confirmed.fix: Call GlobalVariablesFlush() after setting kill. Save eqpeak whenever it rises by more than about 0.5% (throttled), then flush. Make ResetKillLatch one-shot by writing a GV marker with the time of the reset, or warn loudly in OnInit when it is true.
confirmed.reason: The MQL5 GlobalVariablesFlush reference says the terminal writes global variables when it closes and that data can be lost in a sudden failure. The code calls GlobalVariableSet("kill",1) at 1324 with no GlobalVariablesFlush anywhere (grep confirms). eqpeak is written only in OnDeinit (379), which does not run on a crash. A hard reboot can therefore lose a just-fired kill latch and restore an old, lower peak. ResetKillLatch=true deleting both GVs on every init is the documented behaviour of that input, but it does silently disable persistence while left on. This is narrow (it needs a crash), so the severity is minor.
confirmed.fix_final: After `GlobalVariableSet(GvName("kill"), 1);` call `GlobalVariablesFlush();`. In V7AccountGuards (only when PeakKillPct > 0), save the peak when it rises at least 0.5% above the last saved value: `if(g_eqPeak > s_savedPeak * 1.005) { GlobalVariableSet(GvName("eqpeak"), g_eqPeak); GlobalVariablesFlush(); s_savedPeak = g_eqPeak; }`. In OnInit, when ResetKillLatch is true, print a warning that the kill latch will not persist while ResetKillLatch=true, or make the reset one-shot by saving the latch timestamp and clearing only latches older than the first init that saw ResetKillLatch=true.

confirmed.title: Flatten paths retry every tick with no backoff or trade-mode check, flooding the server with close requests
confirmed.detail: V7GridExits (basket and time stop), kill, daily halt, session-end and g_haltFlatten all call CloseAll on every tick while positions remain. Each call makes up to 3 OrderSend attempts per position with `Sleep(100)` between failures, and prints `CLOSE FAIL` and the `>>> TIME STOP` / `>>> BASKET STOP` line each time. Nothing checks SYMBOL_TRADE_MODE, TERMINAL_TRADE_ALLOWED or MQL_TRADE_ALLOWED first. The daily-loss baseline is balance only, so float carried over midnight can trip the day stop on the first tick of the day, right in the rollover window when spreads are widest and some brokers disable trading.
confirmed.failure_scenario: MaxHoldSec expires at 23:59:30 server time, while the broker rejects trades with MARKET_CLOSED/TRADE_DISABLED until 00:05 and quotes keep ticking. With 2 sides x 3 positions, each tick sends up to 18 rejected requests and blocks OnTick for over 1 s of Sleep. Over 5 minutes that is thousands of requests and journal lines. Anti-flood rules (TOO_MANY_REQUESTS) or broker dealing may then restrict the account just when it needs to close.
confirmed.fix: After CloseAll returns fails>0, store `g_nextCloseTry[side]=TimeCurrent()+2`, then back off exponentially up to about 30 s. Skip the attempt (log once) when `SymbolInfoInteger(g_sym,SYMBOL_TRADE_MODE)==SYMBOL_TRADE_MODE_DISABLED || !TerminalInfoInteger(TERMINAL_TRADE_ALLOWED) || !MQLInfoInteger(MQL_TRADE_ALLOWED)`.
confirmed.reason: CloseAll (1103-1121) makes up to 3 OrderSend attempts per position, with Sleep(100) after every non-INVALID_FILL failure. Every flatten path (V7GridExits basket and time stop, kill, day halt, session end, g_haltFlatten, Friday) calls it on every tick while positions remain. The BASKET STOP and TIME STOP lines print each time. Nothing checks SYMBOL_TRADE_MODE, TERMINAL_TRADE_ALLOWED or MQL_TRADE_ALLOWED (grep confirms). In one tick V7GridExits and V7AccountGuards can both call CloseAll on the same side, doubling the attempts. With 6 positions that is 18+ requests and about 1.8 s of Sleep per tick while the broker rejects trades but quotes keep coming. The midnight sub-point is also right: g_dayBal is balance only, so a float carried across midnight counts as the new day's loss. This is a robustness issue rather than a logic error, so minor.
confirmed.fix_final: Add `datetime g_nextCloseTry[2]; int g_closeBackoff[2];`. Write a wrapper `int CloseSide(int k)`: if TimeCurrent() < g_nextCloseTry[k], return -1. If `SymbolInfoInteger(g_sym, SYMBOL_TRADE_MODE) == SYMBOL_TRADE_MODE_DISABLED || !TerminalInfoInteger(TERMINAL_TRADE_ALLOWED) || !MQLInfoInteger(MQL_TRADE_ALLOWED)`, log once and back off. Otherwise `int f = CloseAll(magic)`. If f > 0, `g_closeBackoff[k] = MathMin(MathMax(2, g_closeBackoff[k] * 2), 30); g_nextCloseTry[k] = TimeCurrent() + g_closeBackoff[k];`, else reset the backoff to 0. Use CloseSide in every flatten path, and print the STOP/flatten lines only on the first trigger or when a retry is actually sent.

confirmed.title: SL/TP prices are rounded to digits, not to tick size, so they fail on instruments where tick size is larger than point
confirmed.detail: `double ND(double v) { return NormalizeDouble(v, g_digits); }` is the only price normalisation. BrokerSL, StopPrice, ClampTP and the TP calculations all use it. EnsureSL and SetTP compare with a tolerance of `<= g_point`. The research doc (section 4) recommends moving to XAUUSD or index CFDs, where SYMBOL_TRADE_TICK_SIZE is often larger than SYMBOL_POINT (for example tick 0.25 or 0.5 on 2-digit indices, or 0.05 on some gold feeds).
confirmed.failure_scenario: On an index CFD with tick size 0.25, BrokerSL returns 4567.13. Every L1 and add returns INVALID_PRICE/INVALID_STOPS, so MarketSend drops TP, then SL, and falls back to a naked position. EnsureSL and HealTP then retry every 60 s per ticket and fail forever, so the broker-side SL (the disconnect insurance) never exists.
confirmed.fix: `double NP(double p){ double ts=SymbolInfoDouble(g_sym,SYMBOL_TRADE_TICK_SIZE); return ts>0 ? ND(MathRound(p/ts)*ts) : ND(p); }`. Use NP for every TP/SL/stop price, and compare with `< 0.5*ts` in SetTP, EnsureSL and HealTP.
confirmed.reason: ND (975) rounds to SYMBOL_DIGITS only, and every SL, TP and stop price goes through it (BrokerSL, StopPrice, ClampTP, the TP math). The code reads SYMBOL_TRADE_TICK_SIZE only in RiskPreflight and FitLayers. Where tick size is larger than point, an unaligned SL or TP gets INVALID_STOPS. MarketSend then drops the TP, then the SL, and the position opens without either. EnsureSL and HealTP fail every 60 s after that, so the broker-side SL never exists. This is latent: on the current FX symbol tick size equals point and nothing goes wrong, and the 'pip = 10 points' convention is FX-specific anyway. It becomes real on the index CFDs that section 4 of the research doc names as the next instrument to test.
confirmed.fix_final: `double NP(double p) { double ts = SymbolInfoDouble(g_sym, SYMBOL_TRADE_TICK_SIZE); return (ts > 0) ? ND(MathRound(p / ts) * ts) : ND(p); }`. Use NP in place of ND for every SL, TP and stop price (BrokerSL, StopPrice, ClampTP floor/ceil, OpenLayer1/TryAddLayer/HealTP TPs). In SetTP, EnsureSL and HealTP replace the `<= g_point` tolerance with `< 0.5 * MathMax(ts, g_point)`.

confirmed.title: OpenOnStart force-open fires the first time it is allowed, not on load, and it skips the STRETCH signal
confirmed.detail: `bool forceStart = (OpenOnStart && !s_startupOpened && bCount == 0 && sCount == 0);` is only consumed when `openOK` passes (`if(forceStart) s_startupOpened = true;` sits inside `if(openOK)`). If the load-time bar is blocked (news, session, spread, halt), or the EA restarts with grids open, the force is held back and fires on a later bar once both sides are flat. It then skips the time filter and, through `if(EntryMode == ENTRY_STRETCH && !forceStart)`, the stretch signal, opening both sides.
confirmed.failure_scenario: OpenOnStart is left true in production with STRETCH mode. The terminal restarts at 03:00 with a BUY grid open. At 09:47 both grids are flat on a bar outside AllowedHours. forceStart opens a BUY and a SELL grid with no stretch signal and outside the time filter, which is not what the mode is meant to do.
confirmed.fix: Use the force once on the first evaluated bar after load: set s_startupOpened=true when the bar logic first runs, or when bCount+sCount>0 at load. Keep the STRETCH gating, or document that it is bypassed.
confirmed.reason: `s_startupOpened` is set only inside `if(openOK)` (618-619). If the first bar after load is blocked by news, spread, margin or session, or grids are already open at load (bCount or sCount > 0), the force stays armed. It fires on a later bar when both sides are flat, bypassing the time filter and, via `EntryMode == ENTRY_STRETCH && !forceStart` (599), the STRETCH signal. The input says 'immediately on load' and the comment at 574 says 'bypassing ONLY the time filter'; the code does neither. Skipping STRETCH is arguably needed for a 1 BUY + 1 SELL smoke test, but the delayed firing is not intended. It is a smoke-test input, off by default, so minor.
confirmed.fix_final: Consume the force on the first evaluated bar: compute `bool forceStart = (OpenOnStart && !s_startupOpened && bCount == 0 && sCount == 0);` then set `s_startupOpened = true;` straight away, before the openOK test, so it is consumed whatever happens on that bar, including when grids are already open. Update the input and the 574 comment to say it also bypasses the STRETCH signal.

confirmed.title: In HF mode grid P/L stats double-count the previous grid; grids flattened by the kill latch are never counted
confirmed.detail: `datetime from = (fromTime > 0) ? (fromTime - 60) : (TimeCurrent() - 86400);` includes every OUT deal of the same magic from the 60 s before the grid started. With EntryTF=M1 a side usually reopens within 60 s of its previous close, which happens on TP, time stop or basket stop. Separately, while g_kill is set V7AccountGuards always returns false, so the 'GRID CLOSED' detection at lines 521-536 never runs for the grids the kill flattened.
confirmed.failure_scenario: The BUY grid is time-stopped at 10:00:31 for -$1.10. A new BUY L1 opens at 10:01:00, and g_buyGridStart is set at 10:01:00 on the next tick. It closes at TP for +$0.20. RecentPnL from 10:00:00 returns -$0.90, which records a loss and double-counts -$1.10 in g_sessionPnL. Panel W/L and Sess $ become unreliable as live performance figures.
confirmed.fix: Record each side's last close time and use `from = MathMax(fromTime - 60, g_lastClose[side] + 1)`. Better, only count OUT deals whose DEAL_POSITION_ID belongs to a position whose IN deal is at or after the grid's L1. Run the closed-grid detection before the V7AccountGuards early return.
confirmed.reason: RecentPnL (1056) selects from `fromTime - 60` and counts every OUT deal (and the IN commission) of that magic in the window. g_buyGridStart is set on the tick after L1 appears (515). With EntryTF=M1 a side often reopens within 60 s of a TP, time stop or basket stop, so the previous grid's closing deals are counted again in the next grid's P/L, distorting W/L and g_sessionPnL. Kill-flattened grids: V7AccountGuards returns false on every tick while g_kill is set (1328-1332), so OnTick never reaches the closed-grid detection at 521-536. Those grids are never counted until a restart, which resets the statics to -1 and loses them for good. Other flatten paths (day halt, session end) do get counted once flat, because the guard then returns true. Only the stats are affected; trading is not.
confirmed.fix_final: Add `datetime g_lastClose[2];`. In the closed-grid detection set g_lastClose[side] = TimeCurrent(). In RecentPnL use `datetime from = (fromTime > 0) ? (datetime)MathMax(fromTime - 60, g_lastClose[side] + 1) : TimeCurrent() - 86400;`. More robust: count only deals whose DEAL_POSITION_ID belongs to an IN deal at or after the grid's L1 time. Move the ReadGrid and closed-grid detection block above the `if(!V7AccountGuards())` early return, or run it inside the kill branch before returning.

confirmed.title: MaxBasketRiskPct is silently ignored when StopPips=0, and StopPips is not checked against spread or stops level
confirmed.detail: `if(StopPips <= 0) return MaxLayers;` means a user who sets MaxBasketRiskPct=3.5 but forgets StopPips gets the full MaxLayers ladder (default 18, LotIncrement 0.07, MaxTotalLots 8.0) with no budget. OnInit only rejects negative values. A StopPips smaller than the spread, or a broker SL closer than SYMBOL_TRADE_STOPS_LEVEL, is also accepted.
confirmed.failure_scenario: $100 account with MaxBasketRiskPct=3.5, StopPips=0 and the other inputs at defaults. The startup log prints no ladder-fit line and the EA runs the uncapped v6 ladder, which the PREFLIGHT shows costs many times the balance. With StopPips=1 on a 1.2-pip spread, every grid is basket-stopped on the tick after it opens.
confirmed.fix: In OnInit: `if(MaxBasketRiskPct > 0 && StopPips <= 0) { Print("FATAL: MaxBasketRiskPct requires StopPips > 0"); return INIT_PARAMETERS_INCORRECT; }`. Also require `StopPips*10 > SYMBOL_SPREAD + SYMBOL_TRADE_STOPS_LEVEL` and `BrokerSLBufferPips*10 >= SYMBOL_TRADE_STOPS_LEVEL`, or at least warn.
confirmed.reason: `if(StopPips <= 0) return MaxLayers;` (1246) ignores MaxBasketRiskPct without a word. OnInit (241-247) rejects only negative values, and the ladder-fit line prints only when StopPips > 0, so a config with Budget=3.5% and Stop=0 runs the full uncapped v6 ladder. Nothing checks StopPips against spread or SYMBOL_TRADE_STOPS_LEVEL either. With StopPips at or below the spread, a BUY filled at ask meets `bid <= fill - StopPips` on the next tick, and FitLayers still returns 1. This is input validation, so minor.
confirmed.fix_final: In OnInit: `if(MaxBasketRiskPct > 0 && StopPips <= 0) { Print("FATAL: MaxBasketRiskPct requires StopPips > 0. Aborting."); return INIT_PARAMETERS_INCORRECT; }`. Then `long spr = SymbolInfoInteger(g_sym, SYMBOL_SPREAD), lvl = SymbolInfoInteger(g_sym, SYMBOL_TRADE_STOPS_LEVEL); if(StopPips > 0 && StopPips * 10.0 <= spr + lvl) PrintFormat("!!! WARNING: StopPips %.1f <= spread+stops level (%d pts): grids will stop out immediately", StopPips, (int)(spr + lvl)); if(StopPips > 0 && (StopPips + BrokerSLBufferPips) * 10.0 < lvl) Print("!!! WARNING: broker SL is inside the stops level and will be rejected");`

confirmed.title: With ResetHaltOnInit=true (the default), a restart mid-flatten abandons an unfinished basket stop
confirmed.detail: g_haltFlatten is only restored when `g_halt && PosCount(...)>0` (line 315), and the default `ResetHaltOnInit = true` clears g_halt first (`g_halt = false; ... GlobalVariableDel(...)`). The leftover positions go back to normal management and TryAddLayer can add to them. The basket stop only fires again if the remaining float is still at or above EmergencyCloseDD_Pct.
confirmed.failure_scenario: EmergencyCloseDD fires at 30%. A connection drop, which is a common reason for both the close failures and a restart, leaves 3 of 8 positions open. The terminal is restarted. g_halt is cleared, the remaining -12% float is below the threshold, and the grid keeps averaging while the opposite grid can open again.
confirmed.fix: Save an unfinished-flatten flag separately (GV "haltFlatten", set when g_haltFlatten becomes true and cleared when flat). Restore it on every init, whatever ResetHaltOnInit says, while EA positions exist.
confirmed.reason: g_haltFlatten is restored only when `g_halt && positions > 0` (315). With the default ResetHaltOnInit=true, lines 288-294 clear g_halt (and its GVs) first. After a terminal restart in the middle of a flatten (g_haltFlatten is a plain global and not persisted), the leftover positions go back to normal management, TryAddLayer can add to them, and the basket stop re-fires only if the remaining float is again >= EmergencyCloseDD_Pct. ResetHaltOnInit is meant to re-enable NEW grids, and it should not drop an unfinished close, which is the v6.12 bug the v6.13 header says was fixed. This is a v6.13 path, not v7, and needs a restart mid-flatten, so minor.

Where it clears (line 404) add `GlobalVariableDel(GvName("haltFlatten"));`. Unfinished basket-stop flatten restored -> closing remaining EA positions"); } else if(GlobalVariableCheck(GvName("haltFlatten"))) GlobalVariableDel(GvName("haltFlatten"));`

confirmed.title: L1's broker SL is set from the requested price, not the fill; fallback tickets can run without an SL for up to 60 s
confirmed.detail: `double sl = (StopPips > 0) ? BrokerSL(type, price) : 0.0;` uses the ask/bid read before MarketSend. MarketSend fetches the price again, and the fill can slip. Later layers use `BrokerSL(type, firstPx)` from the actual L1 fill, so L1's SL differs from the others until the next EnsureSL. EnsureSL only runs in the 60-s HealTP block, so positions opened by the no-SL fallback (`req.tp = 0; req.sl = 0;`) carry no broker SL for up to 60 s. FitLayers sizes the budget at StopPips and leaves out the BrokerSLBufferPips that applies when the virtual stop fails.
confirmed.failure_scenario: A BUY L1 fills 4 points better than requested, so its SL is 4 points higher than L2's. During a disconnect, the case the broker SL exists for, L1 is stopped first and L2 survives. On reconnect the oldest ticket is L2, which leads to the M1 re-anchor. When the virtual stop is missed, the realised basket loss on a 2-layer 10-pip ladder is about 30% above MaxBasketRiskPct because of the 2-pip buffer.
confirmed.fix: Call EnsureSL(type, magic) right after a successful OpenLayer1, and right after any add whose SL was dropped. Optionally include BrokerSLBufferPips (plus stop slippage) in FitLayers' `dist`.
confirmed.reason: OpenLayer1 builds L1's SL from `price`, the ask/bid read BEFORE MarketSend (678, 687). MarketSend re-reads the tick and can fill up to deviation=30 points (3 pips) away. TryAddLayer and EnsureSL anchor to L1's actual POSITION_PRICE_OPEN, so L1's broker SL can differ from the other tickets by the slippage, which can be larger than the 2-pip buffer. EnsureSL runs only inside the 60-s heal block (542-549), so it corrects this, and adds any SL missing after the no-SL fallback (874-875), only up to 60 s later. During that window there is no disconnect insurance. One sub-point is a design choice rather than a defect: FitLayers leaving BrokerSLBufferPips out of its budget. The virtual stop is the primary stop and RiskSlipPts models its slippage.
confirmed.fix_final: After a successful send in OpenLayer1 (`if(MarketSend(...)) { ... }`) call `if(StopPips > 0) EnsureSL(type, magic);`. EnsureSL re-reads the L1 fill via GridTimes and fixes the SL straight away. If the position list lags and the new ticket is not visible yet, it is a no-op and the 60-s heal still applies. Do the same in TryAddLayer after SetTP: `if(StopPips > 0) EnsureSL(type, magic);`. Optionally state in the docs, or include as an input option, that the budget assumes the virtual stop fires; a missed virtual stop costs up to BrokerSLBufferPips more per layer.

confirmed.title: _acct_guards skips the kill latch and daily-loss check whenever the EA is flat, so losses realized by a stop are never seen
confirmed.detail: `_acct_guards` begins with `if S[N0] + S[N1] == 0: return`. The EA's V7AccountGuards computes `eq = GridEquity()` on every tick whether or not positions are open. It sets `g_kill` or `g_dayHalt` as soon as equity (= balance when flat) is past the limit, and `sessOK = InSession() && !g_dayHalt && !g_kill` then blocks new grids. In the simulator, a loss realized by a StopPips stop, a time stop, or a TP/stop that leaves the account flat is not tested. The next entry bar opens a new grid, because DAYHALT and KILL are still 0. If that grid TPs inside a segment before the next waypoint check, the account is flat again and the guard is skipped again. In EntryMode=1 only one side is ever open, so every stop leaves the account flat. That is the main v7 configuration, and optimize_hf searches DailyLossPct over {3, 5, 8} with PeakKillPct=25.
confirmed.failure_scenario: Tested in scratchpad/review_sim/exp1_daily_flat.py and exp2_kill_flat_and_overshoot.py. Setup: $1000, 0.1 lot BUY, StopPips=10, DailyLossPct=0.5 (or PeakKillPct=0.5). The stop realizes -$10 (-1%), which crosses the limit, and leaves the account flat. Then 10 bars, each spiking +6 pips first. Sim: daily_stops=0 (killed=0), grids_opened=11, wins=10, final_balance=1040. EA: halts or latches at the stop, grids_opened=1, balance 990.
confirmed.reason: `_acct_guards` returns at once when N0+N1==0 (bgrid_bt.py:714). The EA's V7AccountGuards (mq5:1306-1344) computes GridEquity() = balance + float on every tick, flat or not, and sets g_kill or g_dayHalt, which then blocks entries through sessOK (mq5:572). I reproduced this in review_verify/s1.py: $1000, 0.1-lot stretch BUY, StopPips=10, then 10 bars that each TP a fresh BUY. With DailyLossPct=0.5 or PeakKillPct=0.5 the sim gives daily_stops=0, killed=0, grids_opened=11, wins=10, balance 1040. With the early return removed (scratch copy fix1) it gives grids_opened=1, balance 990, and daily_stops=1 or killed=1, which matches the EA. All tests in test_bt.py still pass with the fix. One nuance: if a later grid stays open past a waypoint while equity is still under the limit, the latch fires late rather than never. A grid that TPs before the first waypoint can lift balance back above the limit, though, and then the breach is missed entirely. The kill flag feeds optimize_hf's score (ruin), so a missed latch also mis-scores configs. Small wording error in the finding: in EntryMode=1 both sides can be open at the same time (a later opposite signal), but usually only one is.
confirmed.fix_final: In bgrid_bt.py `_acct_guards`, delete the first two lines (`if S[N0] + S[N1] == 0:` / `return`). The rest stays as is: when flat, `_lin` gives A=B=0, so eq == S[BAL], and `_close_side` on an empty side returns 0.0 and changes nothing. The bar-open call (line 602) then catches a flat breach before the entry block, and the waypoint calls (line 679, gated on p[53]>0 or p[44]>0) catch it intrabar. The existing `if S[KILL] > 0 and flat: break` keeps working.

confirmed.title: Kill latch and daily loss fill at the next waypoint (the bar extreme), not where the threshold was crossed; adds continue past the limit
confirmed.detail: The guards run only after each whole segment: `if p[53] > 0 or p[44] > 0: _acct_guards(S, wp[k + 1], ...)`. The close happens at wp[k+1]. With the default 4-point path that is the bar's high or low. The basket stop (x1) and stop-out (x2) are solved exactly as linear events inside `_segment`, but the PeakKillPct and DailyLossPct thresholds are not. Grid adds also keep filling inside the segment after equity has passed the limit. The commit message says the guards now match "the EA's per-tick checks", and that is not true intrabar.
confirmed.failure_scenario: exp2_kill_flat_and_overshoot.py: $1000, one 0.1-lot BUY, one bear bar with a low 30 pips down. DailyLossPct=0.5 gives final_balance 970.00, and PeakKillPct=0.5 also gives 970.00. EmergencyCloseDD_Pct=0.5 and StopPips=5 both give 995.00. The EA would exit near -$5, but the simulator books -$30, 6x the limit.
confirmed.fix: Treat both guards as extra linear thresholds in `_thresholds` and `_segment`, the same way as x1/x2. Kill float threshold: x3 = S[BAL] - S[PEAK]*(1 - p[53]/100) when p[53] > 0 and KILL == 0. Daily: x4 = S[BAL] - S[DAYBAL]*(1 - p[44]/100) when p[44] > 0 and DAYHALT == 0. Solve ms = (-x - B)/A in the same loop as k in range(2), and add event codes 6 and 7 that close both sides at ms and set KILL or DAYHALT (DAYSTOPS += 1). PEAK cannot rise while equity is falling toward the threshold, so the value at the start of the iteration is exact.
confirmed.reason: The kill and daily guards run only at waypoint ends (lines 678-679), and the close happens at wp[k+1]. Inside `_segment`, only x1 (EmergencyCloseDD) and x2 (stop-out) are solved as linear thresholds. Grid adds also keep filling inside the segment after equity has passed the limit. review_verify/s2.py, one 0.1-lot BUY and a bear bar 30 pips down: DailyLossPct=0.5 and PeakKillPct=0.5 both end at 970.00, against 995.00 for EmergencyCloseDD_Pct=0.5 or StopPips=5. With a 1-pip ladder (MaxLayers=10) DailyLossPct=0.5 ends at 745.00 with 9 adds, while EmergencyCloseDD ends at 995.00 with 2 adds. PathPoints=3 (the optimizer setting) shrinks the overshoot to 988.03 but does not remove it. The EA checks both guards on every tick, so it would exit near -$5.
confirmed.fix_final: In `_thresholds`, also return x3 (kill) = S[BAL] - S[PEAK]*(1 - p[53]/100) if p[53]>0 and S[KILL]==0, else 1e18. Return x4 (daily) = S[BAL] - S[DAYBAL]*(1 - p[44]/100) if p[44]>0 and S[DAYHALT]==0 and S[DAYBAL]>0, else 1e18. In `_segment`, add these to the immediate checks: `if fl_cur <= -x3:` close both sides at cur, add to STOPLOSS, set KILL=1, continue. `if fl_cur <= -x4:` close both sides, set DAYHALT=1, DAYSTOPS+=1, continue. In both direction branches, loop over the four thresholds (x2, x1, x3, x4) when solving ms = (-x - B)/A. Use event codes 3, 4, 6, 7, because 5 is already the side stop. Handle ev 6 and 7 as `_track`, close both sides at cur (no slip, like x1), set KILL or DAYHALT+DAYSTOPS, then `_track`. Add the same x3/x4 checks to `_jump` next to x1/x2. Between events A and B are constant and equity falls monotonically toward the threshold, so PEAK as of the current iteration is exact.

confirmed.title: Stops and TPs crossed by a spread change are detected only when the next segment moves toward them; BUY stop and SELL TP are missed on a flat or rising tape
confirmed.detail: The BUY stop (`lv = S[FIRST0] - stop_d + hs`, line 335) and the SELL TP (line 329) are evaluated only `if down`. The SELL stop (line 362) and the BUY TP (line 356) are evaluated only in the up branch. The `lv` clipping to `cur` handles an already-crossed level only for the direction being walked. When hs changes at a bar boundary, bid or ask can cross a stop or TP with no mid move. That happens with the per-bar MT5 spread array, the rollover multiplier, or the hour profile. A segment with a == bnd falls into the up branch (`down = bnd < a` is False). Equal waypoints are skipped (`if wp[k + 1] != wp[k]`). So a BUY stop crossed by a spread spike is never triggered on a flat or rising tape. A SELL stop is triggered at once, which makes the error asymmetric. When the stop is caught late, it fills at a later and better price.
confirmed.failure_scenario: exp6_spread_spike_stop.py: StopPips=5, per-bar spread 0 then 140 points (rollover spike) for 3 bars. BUY on a flat tape: side_stops=0. BUY on a rising tape: side_stops=0. BUY on a falling tape: stopped. SELL: stopped in all three cases. The EA's V7GridExits fires on the first spike tick in every case (bid is 7 pips through the stop).
confirmed.fix: Add a direction-independent crossed-level check before walking. One way is at the top of each `_segment` loop iteration, before the direction branches. For each side with positions: `if S[N0] > 0 and stop_d > 0 and cur - hs <= S[FIRST0] - stop_d: close BUY at cur - slip (SIDESTOPS += 1); continue`. `if S[N1] > 0 and stop_d > 0 and cur + hs >= S[FIRST1] + stop_d: close SELL at cur + slip; continue`. `if S[N0] > 0 and cur - hs >= S[TP0] - 1e-9: TP BUY at cur; continue`. `if S[N1] > 0 and cur + hs <= S[TP1] + 1e-9: TP SELL at cur; continue`. Also call `_segment` on equal-price legs, or call the check once in run_core with the new bar's hs before the prev_c -> o move.
confirmed.reason: The BUY stop and SELL TP are tested only in the `down` branch, and the SELL stop and BUY TP only in the up branch. A segment with a==bnd counts as up (line 304), and equal waypoints are skipped (line 674). The inter-bar segment (line 588) is the first place a new bar's hs is applied, and it always runs, but on an up or flat move it cannot see a BUY stop that was crossed by a spread increase. review_verify/s3.py (StopPips=5, per-bar spread 0 then 140 pts, 0.1 lot): BUY on a bull bar is stopped at -7.00 (right), on a bear bar O->H->L->C at -5.00 (too late, at a better price), and on an up-only bar not at all. SELL is stopped at -7.00 in every case. The EA's V7GridExits fires on the first tick of the spike (-7.00). TPs crossed by a spread narrowing are missed the same way. Real-world impact is smaller than the toy cases, because most M1 bars have a down leg that catches it within the bar, and the optimizer's sessions end before the rollover spike. It hits every bar on MT5 per-bar-spread data. A scratch fix (fix3) gives -7.00 in all six cases and passes the tests.
confirmed.fix_final: In `_segment`, at the top of the event loop, after the x2/x1 immediate checks and before the direction branches, add direction-independent crossed-level checks, each ending in `continue`. (a) `if stop_d > 0 and S[N0] > 0 and cur <= S[FIRST0] - stop_d + hs:` `_track`, then `S[STOPLOSS] += _close_side(S, 0, cur - slip, hs, p, t)`, `S[SIDESTOPS] += 1`, continue. (b) `if stop_d > 0 and S[N1] > 0 and cur >= S[FIRST1] + stop_d - hs:` the same for side 1 at `cur + slip`. (c) `if S[N0] > 0 and cur - hs >= S[TP0] - 1e-9:` pnl = `_close_side(S, 0, cur, hs, p, t)`, TPPROFIT += pnl, WINS or LOSSES += 1, `_track`, continue. (d) `if S[N1] > 0 and cur + hs <= S[TP1] + 1e-9:` the same for side 1. Each must `continue` so that A, B and the thresholds are recomputed. This also puts stop before add on the same tick, as in the EA (V7GridExits runs before TryAddLayer). No change is needed for equal-price waypoint legs: hs only changes at bar boundaries, and the prev_c->o segment always runs.

confirmed.title: _fit_layers ignores the slippage drift of add fills, so the realized loss at the stop exceeds MaxBasketRiskPct
confirmed.detail: `dist = stop_d - (k - 1) * step` assumes layer k fills exactly (k-1)*step below L1. In the simulator's own fill model, each add triggers at `LAST - step` where LAST is the previous slipped fill, and then fills at `+slip`. So fill_k = FIRST0 - (k-1)*(step - slip). The real loss of layer k is lot*cs*(dist + k*slip) + lot*comm, while the fit charges lot*cs*(dist + slip) + lot*comm. Only L1, whose fill has no slippage, is priced correctly. The ladder compresses toward the stop and every deeper layer is under-charged by (k-1)*slip.
confirmed.failure_scenario: exp4_fit_slip.py: StopPips=10, GridSpacingPts=20, SlippagePts=5, 0.01 flat lots, budget 0.33% of $1000 = $3.30. The fit allows 5 layers with a predicted loss of $3.25. A straight drop stops out at $3.75 realized, 14% over the budget the module is supposed to guarantee.
confirmed.fix: In `_fit_layers`: `dist = stop_d - (k - 1) * (step - slip)`; `if dist <= 2.0 * hs: break` (a layer whose trigger bid is already below the stop is never reached; this also uses the currently unused `hs`); `add = lot * p[27] * (dist + slip) + lot * p[28]`. Mirror the same change in the EA's FitLayers with RiskSlipPts.
confirmed.reason: Each add triggers at LAST-step, where LAST is the previous slipped fill, and fills at +slip. So fill_k = FIRST0 - (k-1)*(step - slip), and the realized loss per unit for layer k is dist_k + k*slip. `_fit_layers` charges dist_k + slip. The EA's TryAddLayer also anchors on the actual last fill (lastPx, mq5:718), so the same drift exists live. review_verify/s4.py (StopPips=10, 0.01 lots, budget $3.30): slip=5, step=20 fits 5 layers, the fit predicts $3.25, and the realized stop loss is $3.75, over budget. slip=2, step=20 realizes $3.30, exactly the budget, against a predicted $3.10. Only minor because SlippagePts is usually small relative to the spacing.
confirmed.fix_final: In `_fit_layers`: `dist = stop_d - (k - 1) * (step - slip)`. Use reachability as the cut-off: `if dist <= 2.0 * hs + slip: break`. The layer's trigger bid is fill_k - slip - 2hs, so it is reached before the stop only if dist > 2hs + slip. The simpler `dist <= 2.0*hs` is also safe, just slightly conservative. Keep `add = lot * p[27] * (dist + slip) + lot * p[28]`. Optional EA mirror in FitLayers: `double dist = stopD - (k - 1) * (step - slip); if(dist <= 2.0*halfSpread + slip) break;`, with RiskSlipPts standing in for add slippage.

confirmed.title: _build_path waypoint times can go backwards at the close (last leg built to t=1.0, close stamped 59/60)
confirmed.detail: The last Brownian leg is generated with `tb = 1.0` (`a, b, ta, tb = av2, av3, t2, 1.0`), so its interior points sit at t2 + (1 - t2)*j/(npts+1). The close is then stamped `wt[k] = 59.0 / 60.0`. When t2 > 1 - (npts+1)/60, the last bridge point is later than the close. The time-stop and guard checks then see time go backwards, and the next segment's AddMinSec/NoAddAfterSec timestamp is wrong by up to 0.7 s. test_random_path_stays_in_bar_and_is_seeded asserts monotonic times but only checks one seed.
confirmed.failure_scenario: exp3_path_times.py over 200,000 bars: PathPoints=3 (the optimizer's setting) gives 3.16% of bars with a backward step, worst -0.25 s. PathPoints=5 gives 9.35% (-0.50 s). PathPoints=10 gives 25.3% (-0.73 s).
confirmed.fix: Build the last leg toward the close's real time: `a, b, ta, tb = av2, av3, t2, 59.0 / 60.0` (t2 <= 0.95 < 59/60, so all legs stay ordered), and keep `wt[k] = 59.0 / 60.0` for the close.
confirmed.reason: The last Brownian leg uses tb=1.0, but the close is stamped 59/60. The last interior point, t2 + (1-t2)*npts/(npts+1), is later than 59/60 whenever t2 > 1 - (npts+1)/60. review_verify/s5.py over 200k bars: npts=3 gives 3.13% of bars with a backward step (worst -0.25 s), npts=5 gives 9.43% (-0.50 s), and npts=10 gives 25.2% (-0.73 s). This also makes the repo's own test flaky. test_random_path_stays_in_bar_and_is_seeded calls np.random.seed(3) from Python, and that does not seed numba's generator, so the path is effectively unseeded. Its monotonic-time assert failed in 3 of 30 runs of the unmodified `python3 test_bt.py`. Changing tb to 59/60 (scratch fix5) gives 0% backward steps for every npts. Impact on P/L is sub-second, so minor.
confirmed.fix_final: In `_build_path`, change `a, b, ta, tb = av2, av3, t2, 1.0` to `a, b, ta, tb = av2, av3, t2, 59.0 / 60.0` and keep `wt[k] = 59.0 / 60.0`. t2 <= 0.95 < 59/60, so all legs stay strictly ordered. Separately, make the test actually seeded by seeding numba's generator, e.g. through a tiny @njit helper `def _seed(s): np.random.seed(s)` called before `_build_path` in the test.

confirmed.title: Intra-segment events are timestamped at the segment start: hold stats biased low, TPs credited after MaxHoldSec, pacing and cutoff gates too coarse
confirmed.detail: `_segment(S, wp[k], wp[k + 1], hs, p, tk, ...)` passes `tk = ti + wt[k]*60` (segment start). Every event in the segment uses that one t: `_close_side` (hold = t - START), `_open` (LASTADD = t), and `_adds_ok` (evaluated once at segment start). The time stop is only checked at the segment end. A TP reached after the MaxHoldSec limit but before the next waypoint is booked as a win, and its hold time is recorded as the segment start. NoAddAfterSec still allows adds for the whole segment that straddles the cutoff. AddMinSec is measured from the segment start instead of the fill time. With PathPoints=0 (the optimizer's robustness case), segments are 20 s long.
confirmed.failure_scenario: exp7_event_time.py: MaxHoldSec=25. A bull bar where TP = H at the 40 s waypoint. Sim: wins=1, time_stops=0, avg_hold_sec=20.0, +$5.00. The EA time-stops at 25 s near +$0.5.
confirmed.fix: Pass the segment end time too: `_segment(..., t0=tk, t1=ti + wt[k+1]*60)`. Stamp each event at `te = t0 + (cur - a) / (bnd - a) * (t1 - t0)`. Make the hold limit an event: if t_lim = START + hold_sec lies in [t0, t1], convert it to the price m = a + (t_lim - t0)/(t1 - t0)*(bnd - a) on the monotone leg and order it with the other events. Evaluate _adds_ok at te.
confirmed.reason: `_segment` gets tk = segment start (line 673), and every event inside it uses that time: `_close_side` hold, `_open` LASTADD, and `_adds_ok`, which is evaluated once at segment start (lines 305-306). The hold limit is checked only at waypoint ends (line 677). Re-running exp7 (MaxHoldSec=25, TP at the 40 s waypoint H) gives wins=1, time_stops=0, avg_hold_sec=20.0, +$5.00. Under the sim's own linear path the hold limit is reached at 25 s, at about +0.5 pip, so a TP after the limit is credited. L1 START is exact (bar open) while closes are stamped at segment start, so TP hold stats are biased low. AddMinSec and NoAddAfterSec get segment granularity: about 20 s with PathPoints=0, about 5 s with PathPoints=3. Waypoint granularity for the time stop itself is a documented approximation (test_v7_hold_in_seconds accepts 30-40 s). The in-segment ordering (TP before an already-expired hold limit) and the timestamps are real inconsistencies, though, and they bias short MaxHoldSec configs (30/60 s are in the search space) optimistically. Minor.
confirmed.fix_final: Pass both segment times, `_segment(S, wp[k], wp[k+1], hs, p, tk0, tk1, ...)` with tk0 = ti + wt[k]*60 and tk1 = ti + wt[k+1]*60, and also pass hold_sec. Inside, stamp each event at te = tk0 + (cur - a)/(bnd - a)*(tk1 - tk0) when bnd != a. Use te for `_close_side`, `_open` and `_try_add`, and re-evaluate `_adds_ok(S, side, p, te)` before each add event instead of once per segment. Add the hold limit as an event: for each open side, t_lim = START + hold_sec; if tk0 <= t_lim <= tk1, convert it to the price m_lim = a + (t_lim - tk0)/(tk1 - tk0)*(bnd - a), treat it as a candidate event (code 8) ordered with the others, and handle it like `_time_stops` (close that side at m_lim, TIMESTOPS += 1). Keep the waypoint `_time_stops` call for flat legs, which `_segment` skips.

confirmed.title: Time-stop exits (and kill/daily/session/news/Friday market closes) get no slippage while the StopPips stop does
confirmed.detail: `_time_stops` calls `_close_side(S, sd, m, hs, p, t)` at the raw waypoint mid. The L1-anchored stop (ev 5) exits at `cur - slip` / `cur + slip`. Both are market closes in the EA (CloseAll). In HF configurations, time stops are a major exit type, so every one is under-costed by SlippagePts. The fit and the SlippagePts robustness case also miss this.
confirmed.failure_scenario: MaxHoldSec=60, SlippagePts=2: every time-stopped side books 0.2 pip x lots better than the stopped-side model. Over thousands of HF cycles this is a systematic optimistic bias of the same size as the stop slippage.
confirmed.fix: In `_time_stops`: `slip = p[31] * p[37]; fillm = (m - slip) if sd == 0 else (m + slip); S[STOPLOSS] += _close_side(S, sd, fillm, hs, p, t)`. Apply the same adverse shift in `_acct_guards` and in the session, news and Friday closes in run_core if those are meant to model market orders.
confirmed.reason: The behaviour is as described: `_time_stops` closes at the raw mid, while the StopPips stop fills at cur -/+ slip. But the sim consistently uses SlippagePts as overshoot on price-triggered fills (grid adds and stops; see the module docstring: 'filled at the level (+ slippage). Real ticks can jump levels'). Other market orders that are not price-triggered get no slippage either, including the L1 market entry at bar open, which happens on every trade. Treating time-triggered market closes as slip-free is therefore a calibration choice consistent with that model, not a code bug. Whether time-stop market orders slip adversely on average is an empirical question. If the team decides that every market order should pay SlippagePts (as the doc's markout cost model charges 0.3 pip per trade), the change should cover L1 entries and all market closes uniformly, not only time stops.
confirmed.fix_final: Only if the cost model is changed so that market orders slip: in `_time_stops` use `fillm = m - p[31]*p[37] if sd == 0 else m + p[31]*p[37]` and pass it to `_close_side`. Do the same for the session, news, Friday and acct-guard closes, and the L1 open price (`px = o[i] + hs + slip` / `o[i] - hs - slip`).

confirmed.title: Per-bar spread silently overrides SpreadPts/profile/rollover, and final equity is still marked with SpreadPts
confirmed.detail: With `use_sprd`, `spr_pts = sprd[i]`, so SpreadPts, UseSpreadProfile and RolloverSpreadMult have no effect at all. SpreadPts is still used for the final mark-to-market: `hs = p[32] * point * 0.5` at line 683. On an MT5 import, optimize_hf's robustness case `"spread x1.5": dict(SpreadPts=ACC["SpreadPts"] * 1.5)` is a no-op. The std account (SpreadPts=12) is also identical to std_raw minus commission. Open positions at the end are valued at a spread unrelated to the data.
confirmed.failure_scenario: Run optimize_hf robust mode on an mt5_import npz: the 'spread x1.5' row equals 'base' to the cent, so a cost-robustness test passes trivially.
confirmed.fix: Add a scale parameter, e.g. `spr_pts = sprd[i] * p[PI['SpreadScale']]`, or interpret SpreadPts as an additive markup when an array is present. Have optimize_hf scale it. For the final mark, keep the last bar's `hs` from the loop instead of recomputing it from p[32].
confirmed.reason: When `sprd.shape[0] == n`, `spr_pts = sprd[i]` and SpreadPts, UseSpreadProfile and RolloverSpreadMult are all ignored. The final mark still uses `hs = p[32]*point*0.5` (line 683). review_verify/s8.py with a per-bar spread array: SpreadPts 2, 3 or 50, with UseSpreadProfile 0 or 1, all give the same final_balance 1006.9618, and only final_equity changes (979.74, 979.71, 978.30) through the end-of-run mark. So optimize_hf's 'spread x1.5' robustness case is effectively a no-op on mt5_import npz files, and std equals std_raw minus commission. Latent: the EURUSD npz from prep_data.py has no 'spread' field, so the reported robustness results are not affected.
confirmed.fix_final: Append a parameter `SpreadScale` (default 1.0) to PARAM_NAMES and EA_DEFAULTS, and use `spr_pts = sprd[i] * p[PI_SpreadScale]` (index 58) in the use_sprd branch. In optimize_hf robust, use `"spread x1.5": dict(SpreadPts=ACC["SpreadPts"]*1.5, SpreadScale=1.5)`. For the final mark, initialise `hs = p[32]*point*0.5` before the bar loop and delete the recomputation at line 683, so the mark uses the last processed bar's hs.

confirmed.title: Friday-close `continue` skips _build_path, so the random intrabar paths of every later bar depend on Friday settings
confirmed.detail: With PathPoints > 0, each bar consumes RNG draws in `_build_path`. The Friday-flatten branch `continue`s (line 597) before `_build_path` (line 671), so those bars consume nothing. Two configurations that differ only in CloseOnFriday or FridayCloseHour therefore get different Brownian paths for every bar after the first Friday evening. That breaks the common-random-numbers comparison the fixed PathSeed is supposed to provide.
confirmed.failure_scenario: Comparing CloseOnFriday=0 against CloseOnFriday=1 with PathPoints=3 attributes path noise to the Friday rule. Monday-onward TP/stop sequences differ even when no position was open on Friday.
confirmed.fix: Call `_build_path(wp, wt, o[i], h[i], l[i], c[i], npts)` (discarding the result) before the Friday `continue`. Alternatively, seed per bar, e.g. `np.random.seed(int(p[46]) * 1000003 + i)`, inside the path builder.
confirmed.reason: `_build_path` is the only RNG consumer. The Friday-flatten branch `continue`s (line 597) before `_build_path` (line 671), so Friday-evening bars consume no draws when CloseOnFriday=1, and every later path shifts. review_verify/s9.py (random walk, PathPoints=3, session 01:00-23:00 with close-at-end, so the Friday close only takes over the session close's role on the same bar at the same price): CloseOnFriday=0 gives balance 1020.3162 and 670 wins, CloseOnFriday=1/23h gives 1020.4609 and 671 wins. Minor and latent: optimize_hf never varies CloseOnFriday (default 0).
confirmed.fix_final: In run_core's Friday branch, before `continue`, add `_build_path(wp, wt, o[i], h[i], l[i], c[i], npts)` and discard the result. That keeps one draw-set per bar for every config.

confirmed.title: grids_hit_max counts against MaxLayers, not the fitted ladder EFFML
confirmed.detail: `_open` does `if n >= p[6]: S[HITMAX] += 1`. When MaxBasketRiskPct or StopPips trims the ladder to EFFML < MaxLayers, a grid that uses every allowed layer is never counted. So `grids_hit_max` reads 0 for v7 configurations that hit their real cap.
confirmed.failure_scenario: StopPips=10, GridSpacingPts=30, MaxLayers=10: the fit gives EFFML=4. A grid that reaches 4 layers gives grids_hit_max=0.
confirmed.fix: Set `S[EFFML0]` / `S[EFFML1]` before calling `_open` in the entry block. In `_open`, compare `n >= min(p[6], S[EFFML0] if side == 0 else S[EFFML1])`.
confirmed.reason: `_open` counts HITMAX only when n >= p[6] (MaxLayers). `_segment` stops adds at S[EFFML0] or S[EFFML1] (lines 323 and 350), so whenever the v7 fit trims the ladder (EFFML < MaxLayers), n never reaches p[6] and grids_hit_max reads 0 even for grids that exhausted their real cap. Reporting only (no P/L effect). It is not used by optimize_hf, but the v6 optimize.py prints it.
confirmed.fix_final: In run_core's entry block, set `S[EFFML0] = effml` before `_open(S, 0, ...)`, and `S[EFFML1] = effml` before `_open(S, 1, ...)`. In `_open`, replace `if n >= p[6]:` with `cap = min(p[6], S[EFFML0] if side == 0 else S[EFFML1])` and `if cap > 0 and n >= cap: S[HITMAX] += 1`. With StopPips=0, effml == MaxLayers, so v6 behaviour is unchanged.

confirmed.title: Sim never sets the kill latch or the daily stop while flat; the EA does
confirmed.detail: _acct_guards starts with `if S[N0] + S[N1] == 0: return`. A loss realised by an exit (StopPips stop inside a leg, time stop, session close) therefore never trips PeakKillPct or DailyLossPct, because the next check happens with the book flat. The EA's V7AccountGuards (mq5:1321, 1333) has no nOpen condition. It evaluates `eq = GridEquity()` (balance when flat) on the same tick as V7GridExits closes the grid, and latches or halts at once. In the sim the latch fires only if a later grid is still open at some waypoint. A grid that closes inside its first leg is never seen, so the sim keeps trading. The optimiser's score treats killed as ruin, so this undercounts ruin. Direction: sim optimistic.
confirmed.failure_scenario: Verified: BUY-only grid, Balance 1000, ZERO_COST, BaseLot 0.1, StopPips 30, PeakKillPct 2, a 40-pip drop, then bear bars where each new grid hits a 1-pip TP in its first leg. Sim result: killed=0, 31 grids, final $1000. The EA latches at equity <= $980 on the first tick past -2% and stays flat at $980. With DailyLossPct=1 the sim gives daily_stops=0. With a time stop realising the loss, the sim opens one extra grid before halting.
confirmed.reason: _acct_guards (bgrid_bt.py:714) returns at once when the book is flat, and both call sites (bar open, line 602; waypoints, line 679) can only run after an exit has already flattened the side. The EA's V7AccountGuards (mq5:1306-1344) has no nOpen condition. It runs on every tick right after V7GridExits, with eq = GridEquity(), which is the balance when flat, so it latches or halts at once. Reproduced in scratchpad/review_verify/c1.py: a BUY-only 0.1-lot grid (Balance 1000, zero cost, StopPips 30) takes a 40-pip drop, then a series of bars where each new grid hits a 1-pip TP in its first leg. The original sim gives PeakKillPct=2 -> killed=0, 41 grids, final $1010; DailyLossPct=1 -> daily_stops=0; with MaxHoldSec=30 also killed=0. With the early return deleted, all three latch or halt after the stop at $970 (1 or 2 grids). All 16 tests in test_bt.py still pass with the patch. The optimiser scores killed as ruin, so it undercounts ruin.
confirmed.fix_final: In bgrid_bt.py _acct_guards, delete the two lines `if S[N0] + S[N1] == 0:\n        return`. With the book flat, eq = S[BAL] + _lin(...) = S[BAL], which mirrors GridEquity(). _close_side already returns 0.0 for an empty side, so the flatten loops are harmless. Keep the bar-open call (line 602) before the open block so a flat latch or halt blocks that bar's opens; the open block already checks S[KILL]==0 and S[DAYHALT]==0.

confirmed.title: Ladder-fit commission and slippage inputs are not tied to the simulator's cost model
confirmed.detail: The sim's _fit_layers uses the account cost model: `add = lot * p[27] * (dist + slip) + lot * p[28]`, with slip = SlippagePts and p[28] = CommPerLotRT (7.0 for std_raw). The EA uses separate inputs, `RiskSlipPts = 2.0` and `RiskCommPerLot = 0.0`, and nothing maps CommPerLotRT to RiskCommPerLot. For the frozen configs this gate is binding: it acts as an equity floor below which nothing opens. With the EA defaults the floor sits lower, so the EA keeps trading where the sim has stopped. The sim's robustness cases also move the gate: higher commission or slippage stops trading earlier and improves the final result. The EA's preset value would not move. Direction: the EA is more aggressive than the sim.
confirmed.failure_scenario: frozen is_rank1 (StopPips 27, MaxBasketRiskPct 3, 0.01 lot, std_raw). Sim layer-1 cost = $2.72 + $0.07 = $2.79, so fit=0 (no entries) below equity $93.00. EA cost with RiskCommPerLot=0 = $2.72, so fit=0 only below $90.67. Verified on the 2012-2016 run: sim equity stops changing after day 340 of 1393 at $92.984 and is idle for about 4 years. The reported -1.4%/yr is one year of trading. robust_is.csv shows 'commission $10' ending at $93.77 and 'slippage x2' at $93.0-93.6, both better than base ($92.98), because the floor rose.
confirmed.fix: Every preset must set RiskCommPerLot = CommPerLotRT and RiskSlipPts = SlippagePts (see M2). Change the EA side, since it is the side missing the information. Report the sim's idle fraction, the share of days with fit=0, next to CAGR. If robustness runs should vary costs without moving the gate, add separate fit-only params to the sim that mirror RiskSlipPts and RiskCommPerLot.
confirmed.reason: The sim's _fit_layers charges `lot*cs*(dist+slip) + lot*p[28]` from the account model; std_raw is SlippagePts=2, CommPerLotRT=7 (optimize_hf.py:40). The EA's FitLayers uses separate inputs RiskSlipPts=2.0 and RiskCommPerLot=0.0, and nothing in the repo maps CommPerLotRT to RiskCommPerLot. For is_rank1 (0.01 lot, StopPips 27, budget 3%), the sim's layer-1 cost is 1000*(0.0027+0.00002)+0.07 = $2.79, so it stops opening below $93.00. The EA's cost is $2.72, so it stops only below $90.67. Reproduced on the real data with optimize_hf.evaluate(build(is_rank1), IS, daily=True): equity last changes at day index 340 of 1393, at $92.984, with 344 grids. So 75% of the in-sample period is idle and the -1.4%/yr is about one year of trading. 'slippage x2' is also idle from day 340 (final $93.024). This explains why robust_is.csv shows identical results for every seed and for the OHLC path, and why 'commission $10' ends higher than base. The EA cannot read the commission itself, so the preset has to carry it.
confirmed.fix_final: Bridge (make_sets / the v7 preset writer, see M2): always emit RiskCommPerLot = CommPerLotRT and RiskSlipPts = SlippagePts from the account model (std_raw -> RiskCommPerLot=7, RiskSlipPts=2). Optionally have OnInit print the fit-floor equity (the smallest equity with FitLayers>=1) so a mismatch is visible. Sim/report: report the idle fraction next to CAGR (days with no grid and fit=0, or the share of the period after equity last changes). If the robustness cost cases should stress P/L without moving the gate, add fit-only params (e.g. FitSlipPts, FitCommPerLot, defaulting to SlippagePts and CommPerLotRT) that mirror the EA's RiskSlipPts and RiskCommPerLot.

confirmed.title: Set-file writer drops every v7 input, so an HF preset runs the EA with all v7 modules off
confirmed.detail: EA_INPUTS lists only the v6.13 inputs, and build() keeps only known keys: `for k, v in cfg.items(): k = RENAME.get(k, k); if k in vals: vals[k] = v`. All v7 keys are silently discarded: MaxHoldSec, NoAddAfterSec, AddMinSec, StopPips, MaxBasketRiskPct, DailyLossPct, PeakKillPct, EntryMode, ZEntry, ZEmaBars, TrendTMax and LotMultiplier. The EA would load at EntryTF=M15 with no time stop, no L1 stop, no ladder fit, no daily or kill limits and no session, which is a completely different system.

The .set contains only GridSpacingPts, TP_Pips, MaxLayers, News* and MaxSpreadPts. The EA then trades symmetric M15 grids with no exits other than TP.
