Append the v7 inputs to EA_INPUTS in declaration order: ("LotMultiplier",0.0), ("EntryTF",15), ("EntryMode",0), ("ZEntry",1.5), ("ZEmaBars",90), ("TrendTMax",2.0), ("MaxHoldSec",0), ("NoAddAfterSec",0), ("AddMinSec",0), ("StopPips",0.0), ("BrokerSLBufferPips",2.0), ("MaxBasketRiskPct",0.0), ("RiskSlipPts",2.0), ("RiskCommPerLot",0.0), ("DailyLossPct",0.0), ("PeakKillPct",0.0), ("ResetKillLatch","false"), ("SessionStart",""), ("SessionEnd",""), ("CloseAtSessionEnd","false"). Add CloseAtSessionEnd and ResetKillLatch to BOOLS. Convert keys: EntryTF = int(EntryTFMin) (PERIOD_M1=1, M5=5, M15=15), SessionStart = f"{m//60:02d}:{m%60:02d}" for SessStartMin >= 0 (same for the end), CloseAtSessionEnd = SessCloseAtEnd, RiskSlipPts = SlippagePts, RiskCommPerLot = CommPerLotRT. Make unknown keys raise instead of being skipped.
confirmed.reason: make_sets.py is still the v6.13 writer: EA_INPUTS stops at DebugLog and build() silently drops any key not in EA_INPUTS. Running ms.build(frozen['is_rank1']) keeps only GridSpacingPts, TP_Pips, MaxLayers, MaxSpreadPts, NewsBeforeMin, NewsAfterMin and NewsCloseMode. It silently drops EntryMode, EntryTFMin, Ladder, MaxHoldSec, StopPips, MaxBasketRiskPct, AddMinSec, Session, ZEntry, ZEmaBars and DailyLossPct, as well as the FIXED keys (PeakKillPct, NewsPauseLayers, SessCloseAtEnd, ...) that only optimize_hf.build() adds. MT5 fills missing .set keys with the EA defaults, so the EA would run v6-style M15 symmetric grids with every v7 module off. No HF preset exists yet (the only presets are the v6.13 cent ones), so this is a broken deployment path, not a broken shipped preset. It is still the only .set writer, and it fails silently.
confirmed.fix_final: Write v7 presets from `cfg = dict(optimize_hf.ACC); cfg.update(optimize_hf.build(frozen[name]))`. Add every v7 input to EA_INPUTS with its EA default (order in a .set does not matter): LotMultiplier 0.0, EntryTF 15, EntryMode 0, ZEntry 1.5, ZEmaBars 90, TrendTMax 2.0, MaxHoldSec 0, NoAddAfterSec 0, AddMinSec 0, StopPips 0.0, BrokerSLBufferPips 2.0, MaxBasketRiskPct 0.0, RiskSlipPts 2.0, RiskCommPerLot 0.0, DailyLossPct 0.0, PeakKillPct 0.0, ResetKillLatch 'false', SessionStart '', SessionEnd '', CloseAtSessionEnd 'false'. Add CloseAtSessionEnd and ResetKillLatch to BOOLS. Convert keys: EntryTF=int(EntryTFMin) (PERIOD_M1=1, M5=5, M15=15); SessionStart/End=f"{m//60:02d}:{m%60:02d}" when SessStartMin/SessEndMin >= 0, else ''; CloseAtSessionEnd=SessCloseAtEnd; RiskSlipPts=SlippagePts; RiskCommPerLot=CommPerLotRT; MaxHoldSec=MaxHoldMin*60 when MaxHoldSec is 0. Keep an explicit allowlist of sim-only keys to ignore: Balance, Leverage, StopOutPct, ContractSize, SwapLong, SwapShort, SpreadPts, RolloverSpreadMult, VolMin, VolStep, HedgeMarginSum, Point, PathPoints, PathSeed, UseSpreadProfile. Raise KeyError on any other key, and on the meta keys 'Session'/'Ladder' if they were not expanded.

confirmed.title: Sim charges no slippage on L1 opens or on any market exit except the StopPips stop
confirmed.detail: Layer 1 fills at `px = o[i] + hs` / `px = o[i] - hs` (lines 659/665) with no slip. The time stop (`_time_stops`: `_close_side(S, sd, m, hs, p, t)`), daily and kill closes (`_acct_guards`), session close (line 615), news pre-close and Friday close also fill at mid ± hs with no slip. Only adds (`_try_add`) and the L1 stop (ev 5 / _jump) pay SlippagePts. In the EA all of these are market orders (MarketSend / CloseAll) and slip live; only the TP is a resting broker order. The frozen HF configs use MaxLayers=1 and exit mostly by TP or time stop, so SlippagePts barely reaches them, and the 'slippage x2' robustness case is close to a no-op. Direction: sim optimistic by up to 2 x SlippagePts per cycle. At std_raw that is 0.4 pip, compared with a measured gross edge of 0.15-0.5 pip.
confirmed.failure_scenario: Verified: 1-layer BUY grid closed by MaxHoldSec=30 on a flat tape. final_balance is 1000.0 for SlippagePts = 0, 2 and 20 alike.
confirmed.fix: Sim: `slip = p[31] * point`. L1: `px = o[i] + hs + slip` (BUY) / `o[i] - hs - slip` (SELL). Keep the TP on the requested price as the EA does (OpenLayer1 uses tick.ask): `S[TP0] = round((o[i] + hs + tpd) / point) * point`. FIRST0/FIRST1 = px (the EA anchors the stop to the actual fill). In _time_stops, _acct_guards, the session, news and Friday closes, pass `m - slip` for side 0 and `m + slip` for side 1 to _close_side, as ev 5 already does.
confirmed.reason: These fills carry no slippage: L1 at `o[i] ± hs` (lines 659/665), _time_stops, _acct_guards, the session close (615), the news pre-close (623) and the Friday close (593). Only _try_add and the StopPips exit (ev 5 and _jump) apply p[31]. Reproduced: a 1-layer BUY time-stopped at 30 s on a flat tape gives final_balance 1000.0 for SlippagePts 0, 2 and 20 alike. In the EA, all of these are MarketSend/CloseAll market orders. One nuance: against the MT5 real-tick tester without Random delay this is parity, because market orders fill at the tick. The defect is against live execution and against the research's own cost model: HF_GRID_RESEARCH.md calls the std_raw results 'raw-ECN costs (... + slippage)' and says 'slippage x2' leaves the conclusion unchanged. For MaxLayers=1 TP/time-stop cycles that case is effectively a no-op; it only moves the fit gate (see M1).
confirmed.fix_final: `slip = p[31]*point`. L1 opens: BUY `px = o[i] + hs + slip`, SELL `px = o[i] - hs - slip`. _open sets FIRST0/FIRST1 = px, matching the EA's stop anchored on the actual fill. Compute the TP from the requested price as OpenLayer1 does: `S[TP0] = round((o[i]+hs+tpd)/point)*point`, `S[TP1] = round((o[i]-hs-tpd)/point)*point`. For every market exit (_time_stops, _acct_guards, session close, news pre-close, Friday close, and _loss_close for the basket stop and stop-out), pass `m - slip` for side 0 and `m + slip` for side 1 to _close_side, as ev 5 already does. TP closes (ev 2 and the _jump TP) stay unslipped.

confirmed.title: MaxHoldSec fires only at the end of a waypoint leg; TPs and adds in the overshoot are credited
confirmed.detail: The intrabar loop runs `_segment(... wp[k] -> wp[k+1] ...)` and only afterwards `_time_stops(S, wp[k + 1], hs, p, ti + wt[k + 1] * 60.0, hold_sec)`. A deadline that falls inside a leg is applied at the leg's end, at the leg-end price (often the bar's H or L when PathPoints=0). Any TP or add in between still happens. The EA checks `tk.time_msc - oldestMs >= MaxHoldSec*1000` on every tick (mq5:1295) and closes at the deadline. The overshoot is up to 20 s with PathPoints=0 and up to about 13 s with PathPoints=3 (leg lengths are random). That is large next to the 30/60/120 s values the optimiser searches. Direction: sim optimistic, since each basket gets extra time to reach TP.
confirmed.failure_scenario: Verified: MaxHoldSec=30, TP 2 pips, bull bar O 1.1000 -> L 1.0995 (20 s) -> H 1.1003 (40 s). Sim: wins=1, +$2.00 (TP at about 37.5 s). EA: time stop at 30 s at about 1.0999, -$1.00.
confirmed.fix: Split the leg at the deadline. For each open side compute `dl = START + hold_sec`. If `tk < dl <= tk1` (tk1 = ti + wt[k+1]*60), set `f = (dl - tk) / (tk1 - tk)` and `mx = wp[k] + f * (wp[k+1] - wp[k])`. Then run `_segment(S, wp[k], mx, ...)`, `_time_stops(S, mx, hs, p, dl, hold_sec)`, and `_segment(S, mx, wp[k+1], ...)`. Apply the same split to the inter-bar segment prev_c -> o[i].
confirmed.reason: The hold limit is checked only after each full leg (`_time_stops(S, wp[k+1], ..., ti + wt[k+1]*60)`), but TPs, adds and stops inside the leg are solved continuously. A deadline that falls inside a leg is therefore applied at the leg-end price, which with PathPoints=0 is the bar's H or L, and any TP in between is credited. Reproduced: MaxHoldSec=30, TP 2 pips, bull bar O 1.1000/L 1.0995/H 1.1003. The original sim gives wins=1, +$2.00, max_hold_sec=20 (the TP is stamped at the leg start). The same symptom drives the doc's '+245%' artifact (a 30 s stop exiting on the bar's high or low). PathPoints=0 does not emulate MT5 OHLC ticks exactly anyway, since adds and TPs are filled at levels along the legs, so the time stop should be solved on the same continuous path. Prototype fix (scratchpad bt_m4.py): the same bar gives time_stops=1 at 30 s and -$1.00. All 16 tests pass, including test_v7_hold_in_seconds.

confirmed.title: Events inside a leg are stamped with the leg-start time, which skews NoAddAfterSec and AddMinSec
confirmed.detail: _segment receives one time `t` (the leg start) and uses it for `ok0 = allow0 and _adds_ok(S, 0, p, t)` (evaluated once per leg) and for `_open(S, side, fill, lot, p, t)` (LASTADD). Consequences: (a) NoAddAfterSec still allows adds up to one leg after the cutoff, whereas the EA blocks at `tick.time_msc - oldestMs >= NoAddAfterSec*1000`. (b) An add made late in a leg is stamped at the leg start, so the next add is allowed sooner than in the EA, which measures from the newest position's POSITION_TIME_MSC. (c) With AddMinSec > 0 the sim allows at most one add per leg even when AddMinSec is shorter than the leg. (d) TP closes record hold time from the leg start (max_hold_sec=20 where the true time is about 37 s). Direction: mixed; usually the sim is more permissive on adds.
confirmed.failure_scenario: AddMinSec=15, PathPoints=0. An add at about 35 s (leg 20-40 s) is stamped 20 s. The next leg starts at 40 s, 40-20 >= 15, so a second add at about 41 s is allowed. The EA blocks until 50 s.
confirmed.fix: Pass the leg end time into _segment. Stamp each event at `te = t0 + (t1 - t0) * (cur - a) / (bnd - a)`, use te in _open and _close_side, and re-evaluate `_adds_ok(S, side, p, te)` per add event instead of once per leg. If AddMinSec is still pending, add `LASTADD + AddMinSec` as a time event.
confirmed.reason: _segment takes a single time t (the leg start). It evaluates `_adds_ok` once per leg and stamps _open (LASTADD, and START for adds) and _close_side (the hold stats) with t. So NoAddAfterSec can admit adds up to one leg past the cutoff, and a late-in-leg add is stamped early, which lets the next leg's add through sooner than the EA's `tick.time_msc - newestMs` check. With AddMinSec > 0, line 387 caps adds at one per leg even when AddMinSec is shorter than the leg (conservative). The M4 reproduction also shows the TP close recorded with max_hold_sec=20 when the true time is about 37.5 s. A falling bar with AddMinSec=15 gave 2 adds against 40 unpaced, which shows the one-per-leg cap. The direction is mixed, as the finding says.
confirmed.fix_final: Give _segment(t0, t1) and stamp each event at `te = t0 + (t1 - t0) * (cur - a) / (bnd - a)` (te = t0 when bnd == a). Pass te to _open, _close_side, _loss_close and _try_add. Re-evaluate `_adds_ok(S, side, p, te)` at each candidate add event instead of once per leg. Drop the 'one add per leg' latch and instead add the time events LASTADD+AddMinSec and START+NoAddAfterSec as split points, the same way as the M4 deadline split.

confirmed.title: Daily-loss and kill thresholds are checked only at waypoints, not at the exact crossing
confirmed.detail: `if p[53] > 0 or p[44] > 0: _acct_guards(S, wp[k + 1], ...)` runs after the whole leg. The EA checks every tick and closes at the first tick past the threshold. In the sim a threshold crossed mid-leg is acted on at the leg-end price. If a StopPips or time-stop exit happens in that leg first, the crossing is missed altogether (and C1 then skips it while flat). EmergencyCloseDD and stop-out are already solved exactly (x1/x2) in _segment, but these two are not. Direction: sim pessimistic on loss size; it also pays an extra round trip when the halt comes one grid late.
confirmed.failure_scenario: Verified: DailyLossPct=1% ($10) and StopPips=30 on a 0.1-lot BUY with a 40-pip drop. The sim realises -$30 at the stop and halts only on the next grid. The EA halts at -$10 float.
confirmed.fix: In _segment, add the two thresholds as linear-crossing events next to x1 and x2: `x3 = S[BAL] - S[DAYBAL]*(1 - p[44]/100)` (float loss that trips the daily stop, when DAYHALT==0) and `x4 = S[BAL] - S[PEAK]*(1 - p[53]/100)` (when KILL==0). Solve `ms = (-x - B)/A` as done for x1/x2. At the crossing, close both sides and set DAYHALT/DAYSTOPS or KILL, matching the EA's per-tick check.
confirmed.reason: DailyLossPct and PeakKillPct are evaluated only at waypoints (line 678) and at the bar open, while EmergencyCloseDD and stop-out are solved exactly in _segment (x1/x2). The EA checks every tick, so with DailyLossPct=1% on $1000 and a 0.1-lot BUY falling 40 pips it halts at about -$10 float. In the sim the StopPips stop (-$30) fires first inside the leg. Because of C1 the halt is then missed altogether; with C1 fixed it would happen at -$30. The formulas are correct: eq - DAYBAL <= -pct*DAYBAL  <=>  fl <= -(BAL - DAYBAL*(1-pct)), and similarly for the peak. Along a monotone leg the equity peak is at the leg start, so using S[PEAK] at the leg start is exact.
confirmed.fix_final: In _thresholds or _segment, add `x3 = S[BAL] - S[DAYBAL]*(1 - p[44]/100)` when p[44]>0, S[DAYHALT]==0 and S[DAYBAL]>0, and `x4 = S[BAL] - S[PEAK]*(1 - p[53]/100)` when p[53]>0 and S[KILL]==0. Include them in the immediate check `fl_cur <= -x` and in the crossing solve `ms = (-x - B)/A`, as for x1/x2, with new event codes. On the event, call _track, close both sides into STOPLOSS (with the M3 slip), then set DAYHALT=1, DAYSTOPS+=1 or KILL=1. Do not call _loss_close, which sets HALT and BASKETS. Keep the waypoint _acct_guards as a backstop.

confirmed.title: EA forgets a daily stop on any re-init; the equity peak is saved only in OnDeinit
confirmed.detail: OnInit always runs `g_dayStart = 0; g_dayHalt = false;`, so the first tick after any re-init sets `g_dayBal = AccountInfoDouble(ACCOUNT_BALANCE)` and clears a daily stop that has already fired. Re-inits include a terminal restart, an input edit or a chart-period change. The sim keeps DAYBAL/DAYHALT for the whole server day. `GlobalVariableSet(GvName("eqpeak"), g_eqPeak)` is written only in OnDeinit (line 379), so after a crash the persisted peak is stale and the kill threshold effectively loosens. Direction: EA more aggressive than the sim.
confirmed.failure_scenario: The daily stop fires at -5% at 10:00. The user changes an input or the terminal restarts at 10:05. The EA re-bases the day to the post-loss balance and resumes trading the same day; the sim would stay flat until midnight.
confirmed.fix: Persist dayStart, dayBal and dayHalt as GlobalVariables (GvName("dayStart"/"dayBal"/"dayHalt")) when they change. In OnInit restore them if the stored dayStart equals today's server midnight. Write eqpeak whenever g_eqPeak rises (throttled, e.g. at most once a minute), not only in OnDeinit.
confirmed.reason: OnInit unconditionally runs `g_dayStart = 0; g_dayHalt = false;` (mq5:306-307). The first tick then re-bases g_dayBal to the post-loss balance and clears a daily stop that has already fired. This happens on every re-init (input edit, chart change, terminal restart). The sim keeps DAYBAL and DAYHALT for the whole server day. eqpeak is written only in OnDeinit (line 379). In addition, MT5 writes GlobalVariables to disk only at a normal terminal shutdown or on GlobalVariablesFlush(), so after a crash even the kill flag set at line 1324 can be lost.
confirmed.fix_final: Persist the daily state whenever it changes: GlobalVariableSet(GvName("dayStart"), (double)(long)g_dayStart), GvName("dayBal"), GvName("dayHalt"). In OnInit, compute today's server midnight. If GvName("dayStart") equals it, restore g_dayStart, g_dayBal and g_dayHalt instead of zeroing them. Write GvName("eqpeak") whenever g_eqPeak rises, throttled (e.g. at most once per 60 s, and always before a kill check). Call GlobalVariablesFlush() after setting kill, dayHalt and eqpeak so they survive a crash.

confirmed.title: EA guard equity uses the account-wide balance; sim equity is EA-only
confirmed.detail: `GridEquity()` returns `AccountInfoDouble(ACCOUNT_BALANCE) + FloatPnL(MagicBuy) + FloatPnL(MagicSell)`. The kill peak, the daily base and the ladder-fit budget therefore move with deposits, withdrawals and other EAs' or manual trades' realised P/L on the same account. The sim's BAL is the EA's own P/L only. The float is EA-scoped but the balance is not, so the stated 'grid-scoped' immunity does not hold for these guards.
confirmed.failure_scenario: PeakKillPct=25 on an account at its peak of $120. The user withdraws $40, and the EA latches the kill on the next tick with no trading loss. Another EA's losing day trips this EA's DailyLossPct.
confirmed.fix: Use an EA-scoped balance: a persisted start balance plus the sum of DEAL_PROFIT, DEAL_SWAP and DEAL_COMMISSION of this EA's magics (HistorySelect), cached and updated when a grid closes. Alternatively, state 'dedicated account only' and refuse to run (or warn) when foreign positions or balance operations are detected.
confirmed.reason: GridEquity() = AccountInfoDouble(ACCOUNT_BALANCE) + FloatPnL(MagicBuy) + FloatPnL(MagicSell) (mq5:1202-1205). It drives g_eqPeak, the daily base g_dayBal and FitLayers. Deposits, withdrawals, credit and other strategies' realised P/L therefore move all three, while the sim's BAL is the EA's P/L only. A withdrawal of $40 from a $120 peak with PeakKillPct=25 gives eq 80 <= 90, a persisted kill latch with no trading loss. A deposit permanently raises g_eqPeak, so withdrawing it later trips the kill. The code does not claim grid-scoped immunity for the v7 guards (that comment is about gridDD), but the divergence from the sim and the operational hazard are real. Minor.
confirmed.fix_final: Neutralise balance operations while keeping the account-level semantics. Each tick (or throttled), HistorySelect from the last-seen time. For every deal with DEAL_TYPE_BALANCE, DEAL_TYPE_CREDIT, DEAL_TYPE_BONUS or DEAL_TYPE_CHARGE, shift g_eqPeak and g_dayBal by its DEAL_PROFIT. Persist the last-seen deal time. Alternatively, use an EA-scoped balance (a persisted start balance plus the sum of DEAL_PROFIT+DEAL_SWAP+DEAL_COMMISSION over deals with this EA's magics). At minimum, warn in OnInit and on detection when foreign positions or balance operations exist, and document 'dedicated account only'.

confirmed.title: Lot rounding: sim rounds half to even, EA rounds half away from zero
confirmed.detail: The sim uses `lot = np.round(lot / step) * step` (banker's rounding). The EA uses `NormalizeDouble(MathRound(lot / step) * step, 2)`; MathRound rounds half away from zero. Exact halves occur with common LotMultiplier and LotIncrement choices, and there the sim uses one step less. That changes the sim's risk and its _fit_layers ladder relative to the EA. Direction: sim lots smaller, so the sim is optimistic on risk.
confirmed.failure_scenario: Each pair gives sim vs EA lots: BaseLot 0.03, LotMultiplier 1.5, layer FlatLayers+1: 0.045 -> sim 0.04, EA 0.05. BaseLot 0.01 x 2.5 -> 0.02 vs 0.03. BaseLot 0.05 x 1.3 -> 0.06 vs 0.07. BaseLot 0.1 x 1.05 -> 0.10 vs 0.11. Additive 0.01 + 0.015 -> 0.02 vs 0.03. There are 25 such cases in a grid over BaseLot 0.01-0.3 and mult 1.05-3.0. The optimiser's current space (0.01 steps, multiplier 0) avoids them.
confirmed.fix: Sim: `lot = np.floor(lot / step + 0.5) * step` (lots are positive), which matches MathRound. The existing geometric-ladder test still passes.
confirmed.reason: In IEEE doubles, lot/step can be an exact .5 (for example 0.03*1.5/0.01 == 4.5 exactly). numba's np.round rounds half to even, and MQL5's MathRound rounds half away from zero (C round). Reproduced: 0.03x1.5 -> sim 0.04 / EA 0.05; 0.01x2.5 -> 0.02/0.03; 0.05x1.3 -> 0.06/0.07; 0.1x1.05 -> 0.10/0.11; additive 0.01+0.015 -> 0.02/0.03. A sweep over BaseLot 0.01-0.30, mult 1.05-3.00 and layers 2-7 gives 56 mismatches. The proposed fix gives 0.05 and 0.03, keeps test_geometric_ladder_from_001 ([0.01,0.02,0.02,0.03,0.05,0.08]) and passes all 16 tests. The current optimiser space (LotMultiplier=0, 0.01 increments) does not produce exact halves.
confirmed.fix_final: bgrid_bt.py _lot_size: replace `lot = np.round(lot / step) * step` with `lot = np.floor(lot / step + 0.5) * step` (lots are positive, so this equals MathRound).

confirmed.title: Fitted ladder depth is not persisted; a restart refits it from current equity
confirmed.detail: `g_effMaxLayers[k] = (cnt > 0) ? (int)MathMax(cnt, FitLayers(GridEquity())) : MaxLayers;`. The sim fixes EFFML when layer 1 opens and keeps it for the basket's life. After a restart the EA refits from today's equity. That can be deeper than the original fit (for example, the other side banked a profit in the meantime) or shallower. If SYMBOL_TRADE_TICK_VALUE is not ready at OnInit, FitLayers returns 0 and the grid is frozen at its current count.
confirmed.failure_scenario: The BUY grid opened with fit=2. The SELL grid then wins, raising equity, and the terminal restarts. The refit returns 3 and the EA adds a third layer the sim would never add.
confirmed.fix: At OpenLayer1 success, also `GlobalVariableSet(GvName(k==0?"effBuy":"effSell"), fit)`. In OnInit, restore that value when positions exist, and fall back to the refit only if it is missing.
confirmed.reason: OnInit refits the per-side ladder depth from current equity with `(int)MathMax(cnt, FitLayers(GridEquity()))` (mq5:311). The sim fixes EFFML when layer 1 opens and keeps it for the basket's life. After a restart the EA can therefore allow more layers (equity rose, e.g. the other side banked a win) or fewer than the original fit. If SYMBOL_TRADE_TICK_VALUE is still 0 at OnInit, FitLayers returns 0 and MathMax freezes the grid at its current count. This only happens on a restart. Minor.
confirmed.fix_final: After a successful OpenLayer1, also `GlobalVariableSet(GvName(k==0?"effBuy":"effSell"), fit); GlobalVariablesFlush();`. In OnInit, when cnt > 0 and that GV exists, use g_effMaxLayers[k] = (int)MathMax(cnt, GlobalVariableGet(...)). Fall back to the refit only when it is missing. When FitLayers returns 0 because the tick value is not ready, defer the refit to the first tick instead of freezing at cnt. Delete the GV when the side goes flat.

confirmed.title: EA stop anchor and hold clock follow the oldest live position, not layer 1
confirmed.detail: GridTimes returns the oldest live position's POSITION_TIME_MSC and price as `firstPx`, and StopPrice, BrokerSL, EnsureSL, MaxHoldSec and NoAddAfterSec all use it. The sim uses FIRST*/START* for the whole life of the basket. If layer 1 closes alone, the anchor drifts to layer 2's fill, one spacing worse, and the age clock restarts. This can happen when an add's SetTP fails (adds are sent with tp=0) and layer 1 reaches the new TP before HealTP runs a minute later.
confirmed.failure_scenario: BUY layer 2 has no TP after a failed SetTP, and layer 1 hits TP. The remaining basket's stop moves GridSpacingPts lower and MaxHoldSec restarts from layer 2's time. The sim would have closed the whole basket at TP.
confirmed.fix: Anchor the stop to the basket extreme instead: the max open price for BUY or the min for SELL, which is layer 1's fill. Measure age from a persisted layer-1 time in ms, recorded at OpenLayer1 from POSITION_TIME_MSC, or from g_buyGridStart/g_sellGridStart stored in ms.
confirmed.reason: Confirmed with a corrected fix. GridTimes takes firstPx and oldestMs from the oldest live position, and StopPrice, BrokerSL, EnsureSL, MaxHoldSec and NoAddAfterSec all use them. When layer 1 closes without the rest, the anchor slides one spacing (EnsureSL then moves every broker SL with it) and the age clock restarts from layer 2. The stated SetTP-failure path is real but mild, because the price is at the TP, far from the stop, and HealTP closes the rest within a minute. The stronger path is a partial CloseAll failure on the basket stop or time stop in V7GridExits. The CloseAll result is ignored. On the next tick the remaining layers have a further stop and a younger age, so the triggered exit is never completed: this is the half-closed basket that the v6.13 g_haltFlatten fix prevents for the emergency stop. The finding's proposed stop fix does not work: once layer 1 is gone, the max open price of the remaining BUY positions is layer 2's fill, the same as the oldest. It only matters for MaxLayers > 1.
confirmed.fix_final: (1) Store a per-side layer-1 anchor at OpenLayer1 success. Select the new position and set g_l1Px[k] = POSITION_PRICE_OPEN and g_l1Ms[k] = POSITION_TIME_MSC. Persist both via GlobalVariables (GvName("l1PxBuy"/"l1MsBuy"/...)) and clear them when PosCount(magic)==0. Use them, rather than GridTimes' oldest position, in StopPrice, BrokerSL, EnsureSL, the MaxHoldSec and NoAddAfterSec checks, and TTryAddLayer's SL. In OnInit, restore them from the GVs when positions exist, or fall back to the oldest position. (2) Add a per-side exit latch `bool g_exitPending[2]`, set when V7GridExits fires a basket stop or time stop. Each tick, if it is set and PosCount(magic)>0, call CloseAll(magic) and skip that side's adds and opens. Clear it once the side is flat.

findings.title: If the per-side basket/time stop only partly closes, the stop moves to the next layer and averaging resumes (the v6.12 bug again)
findings.detail: V7GridExits ignores CloseAll's return value: `CloseAll(magic); continue;` (basket, line 1291) and `CloseAll(magic);` (time stop, line 1299). Nothing records that the side is stopped, so the rest of OnTick runs as usual: ReadGrid, then `TryAddLayer(...)` at lines 554-558, which only checks `layersOK`. On every tick the anchor is read again from live positions. GridTimes takes `firstPx` from whichever surviving position is oldest (lines 1217-1222). EnsureSL then sets every ticket's SL from that anchor, `double sl = BrokerSL(type, firstPx);`, and nothing stops it moving an SL further away (line 1425). If layer 1 closes but a later layer does not, the virtual stop, the broker SL and the NoAddAfterSec/MaxHoldSec clocks all re-anchor to layer 2. If every close fails, layer 1 stays and the stop re-fires each tick, but TryAddLayer can still add a new layer in the same tick (count < maxL, price at least one step below lastPx). The v6.13 header calls exactly this a v6.12 bug, fixed for EmergencyCloseDD with g_haltFlatten. The new v7 stop has no such latch. The same partial-close pattern exists in the v6.13 pre-news close with NEWS_CLOSE_PROFIT (line 492): once the remainder is negative it is never retried, and adds continue unless NewsPauseLayers is on. The Strategy Tester never produces partial close failures, so backtests cannot show this.
findings.failure_scenario: $100 account, StopPips=10, spacing 75 pts, 0.01 lots, so the ladder fit allows 2 layers (L1 at 0, L2 at -7.5 pips). Price hits L1-10 in a fast move. CloseAll closes L2 first (highest index), then L1 succeeds, or L2 fails 3 times with REQUOTE/PRICE_OFF/TOO_MANY_REQUESTS. Take the case where L1 is closed and L2 is left. Next tick: firstPx = L2, so the stop becomes L1-17.5. Within 60 s EnsureSL moves L2's broker SL from L1-12 to L1-19.5. TryAddLayer adds L3 at L1-15 because count 1 < g_effMaxLayers 2. Realised loss is about 10+10+2.5 pips against a fitted budget of 10+2.5, about 1.8x MaxBasketRiskPct, and it compounds on deeper ladders. If the terminal's position list lags after the close (the code assumes such lag at lines 750-762), the same-tick add can also open a fresh layer straight after a successful stop.
findings.fix: Add a per-side latch `bool g_sideFlat[2];`. In V7GridExits, set g_sideFlat[k]=true on a basket or time hit. At the top of the loop: `if(g_sideFlat[k]){ if(PosCount(magic)==0) g_sideFlat[k]=false; else { CloseAll(magic); continue; } }`. Gate adds: `if(bCount>0 && layersOK && !g_sideFlat[0]) TryAddLayer(...)` (same for SELL), and skip OpenLayer1/EnsureSL for latched sides. Persist the latch in a GlobalVariable. In EnsureSL never loosen an existing SL: BUY `if(cur>0 && sl<cur-g_point) continue;`, SELL `if(cur>0 && sl>cur+g_point) continue;`. Better still, persist each side's L1 anchor price and time when layer 1 fills and use that, not the oldest surviving ticket.

findings.title: No hedging-account check: on a netting account the grids net out, and the stop and layer count stop working
findings.detail: OnInit validates magics, lots and v7 inputs but never checks ACCOUNT_MARGIN_MODE (grep finds no MARGIN_MODE anywhere). On a netting account the BUY and SELL magics share one position per symbol. ReadGrid then always returns count=1, and lastPx/firstPx = POSITION_PRICE_OPEN is the averaged price. So `if(count >= maxL) return;` never fires. Each add moves the average down by step/(n+1), so the next add trigger and the virtual stop `StopPrice(type, firstPx)` both follow price down. Each add's `req.sl` also replaces the netted position's SL with a lower one. In SYMMETRIC mode the SELL L1 just closes the BUY L1 on every EntryTF bar.
findings.failure_scenario: An account opened as netting, which some brokers use by default for some account types, with STRETCH mode and StopPips=10, fit=2. A BUY signal opens 0.01 lot. As price falls, an add fires whenever ask <= average-7.5 pips. Because the average keeps falling, the stop (average-10) is never reached while price falls steadily. Lots grow until margin returns NO_MONEY or MaxTotalLots (default 8.0) is hit. In SYMMETRIC mode with EntryTF=M1 the EA pays a full round trip every minute.
findings.fix: In OnInit: `if((ENUM_ACCOUNT_MARGIN_MODE)AccountInfoInteger(ACCOUNT_MARGIN_MODE) != ACCOUNT_MARGIN_MODE_RETAIL_HEDGING) { Print("FATAL: hedging account required"); return INIT_FAILED; }`

findings.title: Daily loss stop is lost on any re-init, and the day restarts from the already-reduced balance
findings.detail: OnInit unconditionally runs `g_dayStart = 0; g_dayHalt  = false;`. On the next tick V7AccountGuards sees `day != g_dayStart` and sets `g_dayBal = AccountInfoDouble(ACCOUNT_BALANCE); g_dayHalt = false;` (lines 1312-1317). That is the balance at re-init, not at server midnight. OnInit runs on terminal or VPS restart, on any input edit, and on a chart symbol or timeframe change, which by the MQL5 docs calls OnDeinit/OnInit without unloading the EA. Neither g_dayHalt nor g_dayBal is persisted, unlike the kill latch. The input promises 'Flatten + stop for the day'. A second smaller gap: at server midnight g_dayHalt is cleared even if a flatten is still failing (`if(g_dayHalt && nOpen > 0)`), so leftover positions go back to normal management.
findings.failure_scenario: DailyLossPct=6 on $100. By 14:00 losses reach -6%, so the EA flattens and halts with balance $94. At 15:00 the user switches the chart from M15 to M5, or Windows Update restarts the VPS. OnInit sets g_dayHalt=false, the first tick sets g_dayBal=94, and trading resumes with a fresh 6% (about $5.64). The day can end near -11.6%, or worse after several restarts.
findings.fix: Persist the halt: `GlobalVariableSet(GvName("dayhalt"), (double)g_dayStart)` when it fires, and on day detection restore `g_dayHalt = (GlobalVariableGet(GvName("dayhalt")) == (double)day)`. Compute g_dayBal from history rather than current balance: HistorySelect(day, TimeCurrent()+60), then dayBal = balance minus the sum of DEAL_PROFIT+DEAL_SWAP+DEAL_COMMISSION+DEAL_FEE of all deals since `day`. Do not clear g_dayHalt at rollover while nOpen>0.

findings.title: Equity peak is tracked and saved even with PeakKillPct=0, and withdrawals count as losses, so enabling the kill or withdrawing can force an immediate flatten
findings.detail: V7AccountGuards runs `if(eq > g_eqPeak) g_eqPeak = eq;` on every tick regardless of PeakKillPct. OnDeinit always writes `GlobalVariableSet(GvName("eqpeak"), g_eqPeak);`, and OnInit restores `MathMax(g_eqPeak, GlobalVariableGet(...))`. The peak includes transient floating profit. GridEquity is balance plus EA float, so a withdrawal (or another EA's loss) lowers eq exactly as a trading loss would. The same applies to `eq - g_dayBal` in the daily check.
findings.failure_scenario: The EA runs for weeks with PeakKillPct=0 and GridEquity peaks at $130 (balance $120 plus a floating grid). The account later drifts to $100 and the user enables PeakKillPct=20. On the first tick, 100 <= 130*0.8=104, so KILL fires, open grids are flattened at a loss, and the latch persists. Similarly, withdrawing $25 from a $120 account at peak trips a 20% kill, and a $7 withdrawal trips DailyLossPct=6.
findings.fix: Track and save eqpeak only while PeakKillPct>0. Store the PeakKillPct that was active, and reset the peak to current equity when the feature is first enabled. Adjust the peak and the day balance for DEAL_TYPE_BALANCE deals (deposits and withdrawals) found in history.

findings.title: Kill latch and equity peak can be lost on a crash; leaving ResetKillLatch=true turns persistence off
findings.detail: `GlobalVariableSet(GvName("kill"), 1);` is never followed by GlobalVariablesFlush(). The MQL5 docs say global variables are written to disk at terminal shutdown and can be lost on an abrupt failure. eqpeak is written only in OnDeinit (line 379), which does not run on a crash. Separately, `ResetKillLatch` deletes both GVs on every init while it is true, and users set it to true to clear a latch.
findings.failure_scenario: Equity rises from 100 to 125 with no clean deinit, so the saved peak is still 100. The kill fires at 100 (-20%) and positions are flattened. The VPS then hard-reboots before a flush. On restart g_kill=false and g_eqPeak=max(100, saved 100)=100, so trading resumes, and the next kill is at $80 rather than the latched stop. A user who left ResetKillLatch=true loses the latch on every restart.
findings.fix: Call GlobalVariablesFlush() after setting kill. Save eqpeak whenever it rises by more than about 0.5% (throttled), then flush. Make ResetKillLatch one-shot by writing a GV marker with the time of the reset, or warn loudly in OnInit when it is true.

findings.title: Flatten paths retry every tick with no backoff or trade-mode check, flooding the server with close requests
findings.detail: V7GridExits (basket and time stop), kill, daily halt, session-end and g_haltFlatten all call CloseAll on every tick while positions remain. Each call makes up to 3 OrderSend attempts per position with `Sleep(100)` between failures, and prints `CLOSE FAIL` and the `>>> TIME STOP` / `>>> BASKET STOP` line each time. Nothing checks SYMBOL_TRADE_MODE, TERMINAL_TRADE_ALLOWED or MQL_TRADE_ALLOWED first. The daily-loss baseline is balance only, so float carried over midnight can trip the day stop on the first tick of the day, right in the rollover window when spreads are widest and some brokers disable trading.
findings.failure_scenario: MaxHoldSec expires at 23:59:30 server time, while the broker rejects trades with MARKET_CLOSED/TRADE_DISABLED until 00:05 and quotes keep ticking. With 2 sides x 3 positions, each tick sends up to 18 rejected requests and blocks OnTick for over 1 s of Sleep. Over 5 minutes that is thousands of requests and journal lines. Anti-flood rules (TOO_MANY_REQUESTS) or broker dealing may then restrict the account just when it needs to close.
findings.fix: After CloseAll returns fails>0, store `g_nextCloseTry[side]=TimeCurrent()+2`, then back off exponentially up to about 30 s. Skip the attempt (log once) when `SymbolInfoInteger(g_sym,SYMBOL_TRADE_MODE)==SYMBOL_TRADE_MODE_DISABLED || !TerminalInfoInteger(TERMINAL_TRADE_ALLOWED) || !MQLInfoInteger(MQL_TRADE_ALLOWED)`.

findings.title: SL/TP prices are rounded to digits, not to tick size, so they fail on instruments where tick size is larger than point
findings.detail: `double ND(double v) { return NormalizeDouble(v, g_digits); }` is the only price normalisation. BrokerSL, StopPrice, ClampTP and the TP calculations all use it. EnsureSL and SetTP compare with a tolerance of `<= g_point`. The research doc (section 4) recommends moving to XAUUSD or index CFDs, where SYMBOL_TRADE_TICK_SIZE is often larger than SYMBOL_POINT (for example tick 0.25 or 0.5 on 2-digit indices, or 0.05 on some gold feeds).
findings.failure_scenario: On an index CFD with tick size 0.25, BrokerSL returns 4567.13. Every L1 and add returns INVALID_PRICE/INVALID_STOPS, so MarketSend drops TP, then SL, and falls back to a naked position. EnsureSL and HealTP then retry every 60 s per ticket and fail forever, so the broker-side SL (the disconnect insurance) never exists.
findings.fix: `double NP(double p){ double ts=SymbolInfoDouble(g_sym,SYMBOL_TRADE_TICK_SIZE); return ts>0 ? ND(MathRound(p/ts)*ts) : ND(p); }`. Use NP for every TP/SL/stop price, and compare with `< 0.5*ts` in SetTP, EnsureSL and HealTP.

findings.title: OpenOnStart force-open fires the first time it is allowed, not on load, and it skips the STRETCH signal
findings.detail: `bool forceStart = (OpenOnStart && !s_startupOpened && bCount == 0 && sCount == 0);` is only consumed when `openOK` passes (`if(forceStart) s_startupOpened = true;` sits inside `if(openOK)`). If the load-time bar is blocked (news, session, spread, halt), or the EA restarts with grids open, the force is held back and fires on a later bar once both sides are flat. It then skips the time filter and, through `if(EntryMode == ENTRY_STRETCH && !forceStart)`, the stretch signal, opening both sides.
findings.failure_scenario: OpenOnStart is left true in production with STRETCH mode. The terminal restarts at 03:00 with a BUY grid open. At 09:47 both grids are flat on a bar outside AllowedHours. forceStart opens a BUY and a SELL grid with no stretch signal and outside the time filter, which is not what the mode is meant to do.
findings.fix: Use the force once on the first evaluated bar after load: set s_startupOpened=true when the bar logic first runs, or when bCount+sCount>0 at load. Keep the STRETCH gating, or document that it is bypassed.

findings.title: In HF mode grid P/L stats double-count the previous grid; grids flattened by the kill latch are never counted
findings.detail: `datetime from = (fromTime > 0) ? (fromTime - 60) : (TimeCurrent() - 86400);` includes every OUT deal of the same magic from the 60 s before the grid started. With EntryTF=M1 a side usually reopens within 60 s of its previous close, which happens on TP, time stop or basket stop. Separately, while g_kill is set V7AccountGuards always returns false, so the 'GRID CLOSED' detection at lines 521-536 never runs for the grids the kill flattened.
findings.failure_scenario: The BUY grid is time-stopped at 10:00:31 for -$1.10. A new BUY L1 opens at 10:01:00, and g_buyGridStart is set at 10:01:00 on the next tick. It closes at TP for +$0.20. RecentPnL from 10:00:00 returns -$0.90, which records a loss and double-counts -$1.10 in g_sessionPnL. Panel W/L and Sess $ become unreliable as live performance figures.
findings.fix: Record each side's last close time and use `from = MathMax(fromTime - 60, g_lastClose[side] + 1)`. Better, only count OUT deals whose DEAL_POSITION_ID belongs to a position whose IN deal is at or after the grid's L1. Run the closed-grid detection before the V7AccountGuards early return.

findings.title: MaxBasketRiskPct is silently ignored when StopPips=0, and StopPips is not checked against spread or stops level
findings.detail: `if(StopPips <= 0) return MaxLayers;` means a user who sets MaxBasketRiskPct=3.5 but forgets StopPips gets the full MaxLayers ladder (default 18, LotIncrement 0.07, MaxTotalLots 8.0) with no budget. OnInit only rejects negative values. A StopPips smaller than the spread, or a broker SL closer than SYMBOL_TRADE_STOPS_LEVEL, is also accepted.
findings.failure_scenario: $100 account with MaxBasketRiskPct=3.5, StopPips=0 and the other inputs at defaults. The startup log prints no ladder-fit line and the EA runs the uncapped v6 ladder, which the PREFLIGHT shows costs many times the balance. With StopPips=1 on a 1.2-pip spread, every grid is basket-stopped on the tick after it opens.
findings.fix: In OnInit: `if(MaxBasketRiskPct > 0 && StopPips <= 0) { Print("FATAL: MaxBasketRiskPct requires StopPips > 0"); return INIT_PARAMETERS_INCORRECT; }`. Also require `StopPips*10 > SYMBOL_SPREAD + SYMBOL_TRADE_STOPS_LEVEL` and `BrokerSLBufferPips*10 >= SYMBOL_TRADE_STOPS_LEVEL`, or at least warn.

findings.title: With ResetHaltOnInit=true (the default), a restart mid-flatten abandons an unfinished basket stop
findings.detail: g_haltFlatten is only restored when `g_halt && PosCount(...)>0` (line 315), and the default `ResetHaltOnInit = true` clears g_halt first (`g_halt = false; ... GlobalVariableDel(...)`). The leftover positions go back to normal management and TryAddLayer can add to them. The basket stop only fires again if the remaining float is still at or above EmergencyCloseDD_Pct.
findings.failure_scenario: EmergencyCloseDD fires at 30%. A connection drop, which is a common reason for both the close failures and a restart, leaves 3 of 8 positions open. The terminal is restarted. g_halt is cleared, the remaining -12% float is below the threshold, and the grid keeps averaging while the opposite grid can open again.
findings.fix: Save an unfinished-flatten flag separately (GV "haltFlatten", set when g_haltFlatten becomes true and cleared when flat). Restore it on every init, whatever ResetHaltOnInit says, while EA positions exist.

findings.title: L1's broker SL is set from the requested price, not the fill; fallback tickets can run without an SL for up to 60 s
findings.detail: `double sl = (StopPips > 0) ? BrokerSL(type, price) : 0.0;` uses the ask/bid read before MarketSend. MarketSend fetches the price again, and the fill can slip. Later layers use `BrokerSL(type, firstPx)` from the actual L1 fill, so L1's SL differs from the others until the next EnsureSL. EnsureSL only runs in the 60-s HealTP block, so positions opened by the no-SL fallback (`req.tp = 0; req.sl = 0;`) carry no broker SL for up to 60 s. FitLayers sizes the budget at StopPips and leaves out the BrokerSLBufferPips that applies when the virtual stop fails.
findings.failure_scenario: A BUY L1 fills 4 points better than requested, so its SL is 4 points higher than L2's. During a disconnect, the case the broker SL exists for, L1 is stopped first and L2 survives. On reconnect the oldest ticket is L2, which leads to the M1 re-anchor. When the virtual stop is missed, the realised basket loss on a 2-layer 10-pip ladder is about 30% above MaxBasketRiskPct because of the 2-pip buffer.
findings.fix: Call EnsureSL(type, magic) right after a successful OpenLayer1, and right after any add whose SL was dropped. Optionally include BrokerSLBufferPips (plus stop slippage) in FitLayers' `dist`.

verdicts.reason: The code matches the claim. V7GridExits (1291, 1299) ignores CloseAll's return value and sets no per-side state. GridTimes (1217-1222) re-derives firstPx and oldestMs from the oldest SURVIVING ticket on every tick. So once L1 is closed and L2 is not, StopPrice and BrokerSL re-anchor to L2. EnsureSL (1425-1432) then sets every ticket's SL to the new, looser value, because it only checks |SL - target| <= point. MaxHoldSec and NoAddAfterSec restart from L2's open time. TryAddLayer (554-558) is gated only by layersOK, so with count < g_effMaxLayers it averages again. I checked the arithmetic: with StopPips=10 and spacing 7.5 pips, FitLayers gives n=2 by geometry, since k=3 has dist<0. A remnant L2 then has its stop at L1-17.5 and adds L3 at L1-15. Loss is about 22.5 pips x lot against the fitted 12.5. There is a second hole the reviewer did not mention. If every close fails and the next tick bounces back above the stop, `hit` is false, nothing retries, and the grid carries on as if the stop never fired. EmergencyCloseDD has the g_haltFlatten latch for exactly this (header lines 30-32); the v7 stops do not. The pre-news NEWS_CLOSE_PROFIT sub-point is also accurate (line 492: once the remainder's float is below 0 it is never retried), but it dates from v6.13, not v7. The Strategy Tester never fails a close, so no backtest can show any of this.
verdicts.corrected_fix: 1) Globals: `bool g_sideFlat[2];` (zero-initialised). 2) In V7GridExits, right after magic and type are set: `if(g_sideFlat[k]) { if(PosCount(magic) == 0) { g_sideFlat[k] = false; GlobalVariableDel(GvName(k == 0 ? "flatB" : "flatS")); } else CloseAll(magic); continue; }`. On a basket or time hit, set the latch BEFORE closing, whatever the outcome (this also covers position-list lag): `g_sideFlat[k] = true; GlobalVariableSet(GvName(k == 0 ? "flatB" : "flatS"), 1); CloseAll(magic); continue;`. 3) Gate the latched side everywhere: `if(bCount > 0 && layersOK && !g_sideFlat[0]) TryAddLayer(...BUY...);` and the same for SELL with [1]; `if(bCount == 0 && wantBuy && !g_sideFlat[0] && OpenLayer1(...))`; skip HealTP and EnsureSL for a latched side. 4) OnInit: `g_sideFlat[0] = GlobalVariableCheck(GvName("flatB")) && PosCount(MagicBuy) > 0;` and the same for [1] with "flatS"/MagicSell. 5) EnsureSL must never loosen an SL. After the existing equality check add: `double cur = PositionGetDouble(POSITION_SL); if(cur > 0 && ((type == ORDER_TYPE_BUY && sl < cur - g_point) || (type == ORDER_TYPE_SELL && sl > cur + g_point))) continue;`. 6) Recommended: when L1 fills, persist the side's anchor (fill price and time_msc) in GVs, use it in V7GridExits, EnsureSL and TryAddLayer in place of GridTimes' oldest-survivor values while the side has positions, and clear it when the side is flat.

verdicts.reason: OnInit has no ACCOUNT_MARGIN_MODE check (grep finds no MARGIN_MODE, HEDGING or NETTING anywhere). The whole design needs two independent position sets per symbol. On a netting account there is one position per symbol: ReadGrid returns count<=1, and POSITION_PRICE_OPEN is the volume-weighted average. So `count >= maxL` never stops adds, and lastPx and firstPx both follow the average down, which drags the add trigger and the virtual stop with price. In SYMMETRIC mode the SELL L1 sent in the same tick simply closes the BUY L1, so the EA pays a full round trip on every EntryTF bar. This has been missing since v6. It is a missing guard, not a logic bug in the hedging path, and it only matters if the EA is ever attached to a netting account. Even so, a one-line fatal check is warranted.
verdicts.corrected_fix: In OnInit, after the magic check: `if((ENUM_ACCOUNT_MARGIN_MODE)AccountInfoInteger(ACCOUNT_MARGIN_MODE) != ACCOUNT_MARGIN_MODE_RETAIL_HEDGING) { Print("FATAL: a hedging account is required (two magic-isolated grids). Aborting."); return INIT_FAILED; }`

verdicts.reason: OnInit sets `g_dayStart = 0; g_dayHalt = false;` unconditionally (306-307). On the next tick `day != g_dayStart` is true, so g_dayBal becomes the CURRENT balance and g_dayHalt is cleared (1312-1317). Nothing is saved to a GV. On a chart symbol or timeframe change the runtime keeps global variables, but OnInit clears these two itself, so the halt is lost on every reinit reason, not just a terminal or VPS restart. The rollover sub-claim is also correct: at server midnight g_dayHalt is cleared even if positions from a failing flatten are still open, and they go back to normal management (adds and TP).
verdicts.corrected_fix: Move `int nOpen = ...` above the day block. Then in V7AccountGuards: `if(day != g_dayStart) { if(GlobalVariableCheck(GvName("dayStart")) && (datetime)(long)GlobalVariableGet(GvName("dayStart")) == day) { g_dayBal = GlobalVariableGet(GvName("dayBal")); g_dayHalt = GlobalVariableGet(GvName("dayHalt")) > 0.5; } else { g_dayBal = AccountInfoDouble(ACCOUNT_BALANCE); if(nOpen == 0) g_dayHalt = false; GlobalVariableSet(GvName("dayStart"), (double)(long)day); GlobalVariableSet(GvName("dayBal"), g_dayBal); GlobalVariableSet(GvName("dayHalt"), g_dayHalt ? 1 : 0); } g_dayStart = day; }`. Add `datetime g_dayHaltDay;` and release a carried-over halt once flat: `if(g_dayHalt && nOpen == 0 && g_dayHaltDay != g_dayStart) g_dayHalt = false;`. When the limit fires: `g_dayHalt = true; g_dayHaltDay = g_dayStart; GlobalVariableSet(GvName("dayHalt"), 1); GlobalVariablesFlush();`. Optionally, so that withdrawals are not counted as losses, rebuild the baseline as balance minus today's DEAL_TYPE_BUY/SELL deal P/L (profit+swap+commission+fee), leaving out DEAL_TYPE_BALANCE/CREDIT.

verdicts.reason: Line 1318 updates g_eqPeak on every tick whatever PeakKillPct is. OnDeinit always saves it (379), and OnInit restores the MAX (298-299). Switching PeakKillPct on later therefore measures against a peak recorded while the feature was off, which can include old floating profit. That can kill immediately on the first tick. GridEquity is ACCOUNT_BALANCE plus EA float, so a withdrawal, or another EA's realised loss on the same account, lowers it exactly as a trading loss would. That applies to both the peak kill and `eq - g_dayBal`. A 20% withdrawal therefore flattens the grids at a loss and latches the EA. Measuring drawdown from the peak is reasonable in itself; the defects are the tracking while the feature is off and the balance-operation contamination.
verdicts.corrected_fix: Wrap the peak update and its save in `if(PeakKillPct > 0)`. Save the active PeakKillPct in GV "killpct"; in OnInit, if that GV is missing or differs, reset g_eqPeak = GridEquity(). Each tick (throttled), scan HistorySelect(g_lastBalScan, TimeCurrent()) for DEAL_TYPE_BALANCE/DEAL_TYPE_CREDIT deals and shift both g_eqPeak and g_dayBal by each deal's DEAL_PROFIT, so deposits and withdrawals do not count as P/L. Then advance g_lastBalScan.

verdicts.reason: The MQL5 GlobalVariablesFlush reference says the terminal writes global variables when it closes and that data can be lost in a sudden failure. The code calls GlobalVariableSet("kill",1) at 1324 with no GlobalVariablesFlush anywhere (grep confirms). eqpeak is written only in OnDeinit (379), which does not run on a crash. A hard reboot can therefore lose a just-fired kill latch and restore an old, lower peak. ResetKillLatch=true deleting both GVs on every init is the documented behaviour of that input, but it does silently disable persistence while left on. This is narrow (it needs a crash), so the severity is minor.
verdicts.corrected_fix: After `GlobalVariableSet(GvName("kill"), 1);` call `GlobalVariablesFlush();`. In V7AccountGuards (only when PeakKillPct > 0), save the peak when it rises at least 0.5% above the last saved value: `if(g_eqPeak > s_savedPeak * 1.005) { GlobalVariableSet(GvName("eqpeak"), g_eqPeak); GlobalVariablesFlush(); s_savedPeak = g_eqPeak; }`. In OnInit, when ResetKillLatch is true, print a warning that the kill latch will not persist while ResetKillLatch=true, or make the reset one-shot by saving the latch timestamp and clearing only latches older than the first init that saw ResetKillLatch=true.

verdicts.reason: CloseAll (1103-1121) makes up to 3 OrderSend attempts per position, with Sleep(100) after every non-INVALID_FILL failure. Every flatten path (V7GridExits basket and time stop, kill, day halt, session end, g_haltFlatten, Friday) calls it on every tick while positions remain. The BASKET STOP and TIME STOP lines print each time. Nothing checks SYMBOL_TRADE_MODE, TERMINAL_TRADE_ALLOWED or MQL_TRADE_ALLOWED (grep confirms). In one tick V7GridExits and V7AccountGuards can both call CloseAll on the same side, doubling the attempts. With 6 positions that is 18+ requests and about 1.8 s of Sleep per tick while the broker rejects trades but quotes keep coming. The midnight sub-point is also right: g_dayBal is balance only, so a float carried across midnight counts as the new day's loss. This is a robustness issue rather than a logic error, so minor.
verdicts.corrected_fix: Add `datetime g_nextCloseTry[2]; int g_closeBackoff[2];`. Write a wrapper `int CloseSide(int k)`: if TimeCurrent() < g_nextCloseTry[k], return -1. If `SymbolInfoInteger(g_sym, SYMBOL_TRADE_MODE) == SYMBOL_TRADE_MODE_DISABLED || !TerminalInfoInteger(TERMINAL_TRADE_ALLOWED) || !MQLInfoInteger(MQL_TRADE_ALLOWED)`, log once and back off. Otherwise `int f = CloseAll(magic)`. If f > 0, `g_closeBackoff[k] = MathMin(MathMax(2, g_closeBackoff[k] * 2), 30); g_nextCloseTry[k] = TimeCurrent() + g_closeBackoff[k];`, else reset the backoff to 0. Use CloseSide in every flatten path, and print the STOP/flatten lines only on the first trigger or when a retry is actually sent.

verdicts.reason: ND (975) rounds to SYMBOL_DIGITS only, and every SL, TP and stop price goes through it (BrokerSL, StopPrice, ClampTP, the TP math). The code reads SYMBOL_TRADE_TICK_SIZE only in RiskPreflight and FitLayers. Where tick size is larger than point, an unaligned SL or TP gets INVALID_STOPS. MarketSend then drops the TP, then the SL, and the position opens without either. EnsureSL and HealTP fail every 60 s after that, so the broker-side SL never exists. This is latent: on the current FX symbol tick size equals point and nothing goes wrong, and the 'pip = 10 points' convention is FX-specific anyway. It becomes real on the index CFDs that section 4 of the research doc names as the next instrument to test.
verdicts.corrected_fix: `double NP(double p) { double ts = SymbolInfoDouble(g_sym, SYMBOL_TRADE_TICK_SIZE); return (ts > 0) ? ND(MathRound(p / ts) * ts) : ND(p); }`. Use NP in place of ND for every SL, TP and stop price (BrokerSL, StopPrice, ClampTP floor/ceil, OpenLayer1/TryAddLayer/HealTP TPs). In SetTP, EnsureSL and HealTP replace the `<= g_point` tolerance with `< 0.5 * MathMax(ts, g_point)`.

verdicts.reason: `s_startupOpened` is set only inside `if(openOK)` (618-619). If the first bar after load is blocked by news, spread, margin or session, or grids are already open at load (bCount or sCount > 0), the force stays armed. It fires on a later bar when both sides are flat, bypassing the time filter and, via `EntryMode == ENTRY_STRETCH && !forceStart` (599), the STRETCH signal. The input says 'immediately on load' and the comment at 574 says 'bypassing ONLY the time filter'; the code does neither. Skipping STRETCH is arguably needed for a 1 BUY + 1 SELL smoke test, but the delayed firing is not intended. It is a smoke-test input, off by default, so minor.
verdicts.corrected_fix: Consume the force on the first evaluated bar: compute `bool forceStart = (OpenOnStart && !s_startupOpened && bCount == 0 && sCount == 0);` then set `s_startupOpened = true;` straight away, before the openOK test, so it is consumed whatever happens on that bar, including when grids are already open. Update the input and the 574 comment to say it also bypasses the STRETCH signal.

verdicts.reason: RecentPnL (1056) selects from `fromTime - 60` and counts every OUT deal (and the IN commission) of that magic in the window. g_buyGridStart is set on the tick after L1 appears (515). With EntryTF=M1 a side often reopens within 60 s of a TP, time stop or basket stop, so the previous grid's closing deals are counted again in the next grid's P/L, distorting W/L and g_sessionPnL. Kill-flattened grids: V7AccountGuards returns false on every tick while g_kill is set (1328-1332), so OnTick never reaches the closed-grid detection at 521-536. Those grids are never counted until a restart, which resets the statics to -1 and loses them for good. Other flatten paths (day halt, session end) do get counted once flat, because the guard then returns true. Only the stats are affected; trading is not.
verdicts.corrected_fix: Add `datetime g_lastClose[2];`. In the closed-grid detection set g_lastClose[side] = TimeCurrent(). In RecentPnL use `datetime from = (fromTime > 0) ? (datetime)MathMax(fromTime - 60, g_lastClose[side] + 1) : TimeCurrent() - 86400;`. More robust: count only deals whose DEAL_POSITION_ID belongs to an IN deal at or after the grid's L1 time. Move the ReadGrid and closed-grid detection block above the `if(!V7AccountGuards())` early return, or run it inside the kill branch before returning.

verdicts.reason: `if(StopPips <= 0) return MaxLayers;` (1246) ignores MaxBasketRiskPct without a word. OnInit (241-247) rejects only negative values, and the ladder-fit line prints only when StopPips > 0, so a config with Budget=3.5% and Stop=0 runs the full uncapped v6 ladder. Nothing checks StopPips against spread or SYMBOL_TRADE_STOPS_LEVEL either. With StopPips at or below the spread, a BUY filled at ask meets `bid <= fill - StopPips` on the next tick, and FitLayers still returns 1. This is input validation, so minor.

Then `long spr = SymbolInfoInteger(g_sym, SYMBOL_SPREAD), lvl = SymbolInfoInteger(g_sym, SYMBOL_TRADE_STOPS_LEVEL); if(StopPips > 0 && StopPips * 10.0 <= spr + lvl) PrintFormat("!!! WARNING: StopPips %.1f <= spread+stops level (%d pts): grids will stop out immediately", StopPips, (int)(spr + lvl)); if(StopPips > 0 && (StopPips + BrokerSLBufferPips) * 10.0 < lvl) Print("!!!
