verdicts.reason: g_haltFlatten is restored only when `g_halt && positions > 0` (315). With the default ResetHaltOnInit=true, lines 288-294 clear g_halt (and its GVs) first. After a terminal restart in the middle of a flatten (g_haltFlatten is a plain global and not persisted), the leftover positions go back to normal management, TryAddLayer can add to them, and the basket stop re-fires only if the remaining float is again >= EmergencyCloseDD_Pct. ResetHaltOnInit is meant to re-enable NEW grids, and it should not drop an unfinished close, which is the v6.12 bug the v6.13 header says was fixed. This is a v6.13 path, not v7, and needs a restart mid-flatten, so minor.
verdicts.corrected_fix: Where g_haltFlatten becomes true (line 438) add `GlobalVariableSet(GvName("haltFlatten"), 1); GlobalVariablesFlush();`. Where it clears (line 404) add `GlobalVariableDel(GvName("haltFlatten"));`. In OnInit, after the ResetHaltOnInit block and whatever ResetHaltOnInit says: `if(GlobalVariableCheck(GvName("haltFlatten")) && PosCount(MagicBuy) + PosCount(MagicSell) > 0) { g_haltFlatten = true; Print("!!! Unfinished basket-stop flatten restored -> closing remaining EA positions"); } else if(GlobalVariableCheck(GvName("haltFlatten"))) GlobalVariableDel(GvName("haltFlatten"));`

verdicts.reason: OpenLayer1 builds L1's SL from `price`, the ask/bid read BEFORE MarketSend (678, 687). MarketSend re-reads the tick and can fill up to deviation=30 points (3 pips) away. TryAddLayer and EnsureSL anchor to L1's actual POSITION_PRICE_OPEN, so L1's broker SL can differ from the other tickets by the slippage, which can be larger than the 2-pip buffer. EnsureSL runs only inside the 60-s heal block (542-549), so it corrects this, and adds any SL missing after the no-SL fallback (874-875), only up to 60 s later. During that window there is no disconnect insurance. One sub-point is a design choice rather than a defect: FitLayers leaving BrokerSLBufferPips out of its budget. The virtual stop is the primary stop and RiskSlipPts models its slippage.
verdicts.corrected_fix: After a successful send in OpenLayer1 (`if(MarketSend(...)) { ... }`) call `if(StopPips > 0) EnsureSL(type, magic);`. EnsureSL re-reads the L1 fill via GridTimes and fixes the SL straight away. If the position list lags and the new ticket is not visible yet, it is a no-op and the 60-s heal still applies. Do the same in TryAddLayer after SetTP: `if(StopPips > 0) EnsureSL(type, magic);`. Optionally state in the docs, or include as an input option, that the budget assumes the virtual stop fires; a missed virtual stop costs up to BrokerSLBufferPips more per layer.

checked_ok: Stop price sides: the BUY basket stop triggers on bid <= L1 fill (ask) - StopPips and the SELL stop on ask >= L1 fill (bid) + StopPips, the same as the simulator's _segment/_jump (FIRST0 - stop_d + hs etc.).

BrokerSL is on the correct side (BUY below, SELL above) and BrokerSLBufferPips beyond the virtual stop. While the virtual stop has not fired, the market-to-SL distance is at least the buffer, so add SLs are not on the wrong side except after a gap or a failed stop (see M1).
SetTP now sends req.sl = POSITION_SL and EnsureSL sends req.tp = POSITION_TP, so neither modify wipes the other. TP modifies are skipped when within one point, so there is no per-tick modify loop.
MarketSend sl handling: INVALID_STOPS drops TP first, then SL; NO_MONEY aborts; the fallback sends with neither. Adds pass tp=0, so INVALID_STOPS drops the SL directly.
ClampTP uses bid for the BUY TP floor and ask for the SELL TP ceiling, and is applied to L1, the post-add TP and HealTP.

Time-stop clock: tick.time_msc and POSITION_TIME_MSC are both trade-server ms. Negative deltas (fill after last quote) are harmless. Ages are read from live positions, so the clock is correct after a restart.
AddMinSec (newest position time) and NoAddAfterSec (oldest position time) match the simulator's _adds_ok (LASTADD / START).

TryAddLayer checks the ladder depth against g_effMaxLayers, which is set only after OpenLayer1 succeeds. At init it is restored as max(live count, FitLayers(now)), so a restart never cuts a live grid below its current count.
FitLayers matches _fit_layers: tick value / tick size equals the contract size for EURUSD on a USD account, dist runs from the ask fill to the bid stop, and slippage and commission are included.

StretchSignal matches stretch_signal: EWMA alpha = 1-0.5^(1/60), EMA span alpha 2/(N+1) with adjust=False, trend = |c0-c60|/(sig1*sqrt60), reclaim against the open and the previous bar's high/low, only closed M1 bars (index 1), acting on the next EntryTF bar. The difference in EWMA seeding over 1200 bars is negligible.

EntryTF bar logic: evaluated once per EntryTF bar via iTime(EntryTF,0), and on the first tick after a fresh load, as in v6. STRETCH with EntryTF=M5/M15 samples only the M1 bar before each EntryTF open, the same as the simulator.

Kill latch and daily halt keep calling CloseAll on every tick while EA positions remain, and return false so TryAddLayer and opens do not run. New grids are gated through sessOK (InSession && !g_dayHalt && !g_kill).
CloseAtSessionEnd keeps flattening while out of session. InSession handles windows that wrap midnight. OnInit rejects a half-specified or invalid HH:MM.

v6.13 interactions: g_haltFlatten, the emergency basket stop and Friday close all return before V7GridExits/V7AccountGuards, so nothing adds during those flattens. HealTP and EnsureSL are throttled to once every 60 s (no modify spam on FX symbols).

Strategy Tester: Sleep is skipped under MQL_TESTER, the news filter loads the CSV in the tester, and CopyClose/CopyOpen on M1 are available. Partial fills, requotes and position-list lag do not occur in the tester, so M1 and the same-tick add race cannot show up in backtests.
Kill latch persistence: restored in OnInit and written in OnDeinit, independent of PersistStats. On restart with a latched kill and open positions, the first tick flattens them.

Compile-level reading of the v7 code: the specifier and argument counts of the new PrintFormat/StringFormat calls match ([BAR] 13/13, v7 init 14/14, panel HF line 10/10). The types (long time_msc, ulong %I64u, ENUM_TIMEFRAMES/enum inputs, const array size) are valid MQL5.

findings.title: _acct_guards skips the kill latch and daily-loss check whenever the EA is flat, so losses realized by a stop are never seen
findings.detail: `_acct_guards` begins with `if S[N0] + S[N1] == 0: return`. The EA's V7AccountGuards computes `eq = GridEquity()` on every tick whether or not positions are open. It sets `g_kill` or `g_dayHalt` as soon as equity (= balance when flat) is past the limit, and `sessOK = InSession() && !g_dayHalt && !g_kill` then blocks new grids. In the simulator, a loss realized by a StopPips stop, a time stop, or a TP/stop that leaves the account flat is not tested. The next entry bar opens a new grid, because DAYHALT and KILL are still 0. If that grid TPs inside a segment before the next waypoint check, the account is flat again and the guard is skipped again. In EntryMode=1 only one side is ever open, so every stop leaves the account flat. That is the main v7 configuration, and optimize_hf searches DailyLossPct over {3, 5, 8} with PeakKillPct=25.
findings.failure_scenario: Tested in scratchpad/review_sim/exp1_daily_flat.py and exp2_kill_flat_and_overshoot.py. Setup: $1000, 0.1 lot BUY, StopPips=10, DailyLossPct=0.5 (or PeakKillPct=0.5). The stop realizes -$10 (-1%), which crosses the limit, and leaves the account flat. Then 10 bars, each spiking +6 pips first. Sim: daily_stops=0 (killed=0), grids_opened=11, wins=10, final_balance=1040. EA: halts or latches at the stop, grids_opened=1, balance 990.

findings.title: Kill latch and daily loss fill at the next waypoint (the bar extreme), not where the threshold was crossed; adds continue past the limit
findings.detail: The guards run only after each whole segment: `if p[53] > 0 or p[44] > 0: _acct_guards(S, wp[k + 1], ...)`. The close happens at wp[k+1]. With the default 4-point path that is the bar's high or low. The basket stop (x1) and stop-out (x2) are solved exactly as linear events inside `_segment`, but the PeakKillPct and DailyLossPct thresholds are not. Grid adds also keep filling inside the segment after equity has passed the limit. The commit message says the guards now match "the EA's per-tick checks", and that is not true intrabar.
findings.failure_scenario: exp2_kill_flat_and_overshoot.py: $1000, one 0.1-lot BUY, one bear bar with a low 30 pips down. DailyLossPct=0.5 gives final_balance 970.00, and PeakKillPct=0.5 also gives 970.00. EmergencyCloseDD_Pct=0.5 and StopPips=5 both give 995.00. The EA would exit near -$5, but the simulator books -$30, 6x the limit.
findings.fix: Treat both guards as extra linear thresholds in `_thresholds` and `_segment`, the same way as x1/x2. Kill float threshold: x3 = S[BAL] - S[PEAK]*(1 - p[53]/100) when p[53] > 0 and KILL == 0. Daily: x4 = S[BAL] - S[DAYBAL]*(1 - p[44]/100) when p[44] > 0 and DAYHALT == 0. Solve ms = (-x - B)/A in the same loop as k in range(2), and add event codes 6 and 7 that close both sides at ms and set KILL or DAYHALT (DAYSTOPS += 1). PEAK cannot rise while equity is falling toward the threshold, so the value at the start of the iteration is exact.

findings.title: Stops and TPs crossed by a spread change are detected only when the next segment moves toward them; BUY stop and SELL TP are missed on a flat or rising tape
findings.detail: The BUY stop (`lv = S[FIRST0] - stop_d + hs`, line 335) and the SELL TP (line 329) are evaluated only `if down`. The SELL stop (line 362) and the BUY TP (line 356) are evaluated only in the up branch. The `lv` clipping to `cur` handles an already-crossed level only for the direction being walked. When hs changes at a bar boundary, bid or ask can cross a stop or TP with no mid move. That happens with the per-bar MT5 spread array, the rollover multiplier, or the hour profile. A segment with a == bnd falls into the up branch (`down = bnd < a` is False). Equal waypoints are skipped (`if wp[k + 1] != wp[k]`). So a BUY stop crossed by a spread spike is never triggered on a flat or rising tape. A SELL stop is triggered at once, which makes the error asymmetric. When the stop is caught late, it fills at a later and better price.
findings.failure_scenario: exp6_spread_spike_stop.py: StopPips=5, per-bar spread 0 then 140 points (rollover spike) for 3 bars. BUY on a flat tape: side_stops=0. BUY on a rising tape: side_stops=0. BUY on a falling tape: stopped. SELL: stopped in all three cases. The EA's V7GridExits fires on the first spike tick in every case (bid is 7 pips through the stop).
findings.fix: Add a direction-independent crossed-level check before walking. One way is at the top of each `_segment` loop iteration, before the direction branches. For each side with positions: `if S[N0] > 0 and stop_d > 0 and cur - hs <= S[FIRST0] - stop_d: close BUY at cur - slip (SIDESTOPS += 1); continue`. `if S[N1] > 0 and stop_d > 0 and cur + hs >= S[FIRST1] + stop_d: close SELL at cur + slip; continue`. `if S[N0] > 0 and cur - hs >= S[TP0] - 1e-9: TP BUY at cur; continue`. `if S[N1] > 0 and cur + hs <= S[TP1] + 1e-9: TP SELL at cur; continue`. Also call `_segment` on equal-price legs, or call the check once in run_core with the new bar's hs before the prev_c -> o move.

findings.title: _fit_layers ignores the slippage drift of add fills, so the realized loss at the stop exceeds MaxBasketRiskPct
findings.detail: `dist = stop_d - (k - 1) * step` assumes layer k fills exactly (k-1)*step below L1. In the simulator's own fill model, each add triggers at `LAST - step` where LAST is the previous slipped fill, and then fills at `+slip`. So fill_k = FIRST0 - (k-1)*(step - slip). The real loss of layer k is lot*cs*(dist + k*slip) + lot*comm, while the fit charges lot*cs*(dist + slip) + lot*comm. Only L1, whose fill has no slippage, is priced correctly. The ladder compresses toward the stop and every deeper layer is under-charged by (k-1)*slip.
findings.failure_scenario: exp4_fit_slip.py: StopPips=10, GridSpacingPts=20, SlippagePts=5, 0.01 flat lots, budget 0.33% of $1000 = $3.30. The fit allows 5 layers with a predicted loss of $3.25. A straight drop stops out at $3.75 realized, 14% over the budget the module is supposed to guarantee.
findings.fix: In `_fit_layers`: `dist = stop_d - (k - 1) * (step - slip)`; `if dist <= 2.0 * hs: break` (a layer whose trigger bid is already below the stop is never reached; this also uses the currently unused `hs`); `add = lot * p[27] * (dist + slip) + lot * p[28]`. Mirror the same change in the EA's FitLayers with RiskSlipPts.

findings.title: _build_path waypoint times can go backwards at the close (last leg built to t=1.0, close stamped 59/60)
findings.detail: The last Brownian leg is generated with `tb = 1.0` (`a, b, ta, tb = av2, av3, t2, 1.0`), so its interior points sit at t2 + (1 - t2)*j/(npts+1). The close is then stamped `wt[k] = 59.0 / 60.0`. When t2 > 1 - (npts+1)/60, the last bridge point is later than the close. The time-stop and guard checks then see time go backwards, and the next segment's AddMinSec/NoAddAfterSec timestamp is wrong by up to 0.7 s. test_random_path_stays_in_bar_and_is_seeded asserts monotonic times but only checks one seed.
findings.failure_scenario: exp3_path_times.py over 200,000 bars: PathPoints=3 (the optimizer's setting) gives 3.16% of bars with a backward step, worst -0.25 s. PathPoints=5 gives 9.35% (-0.50 s). PathPoints=10 gives 25.3% (-0.73 s).
findings.fix: Build the last leg toward the close's real time: `a, b, ta, tb = av2, av3, t2, 59.0 / 60.0` (t2 <= 0.95 < 59/60, so all legs stay ordered), and keep `wt[k] = 59.0 / 60.0` for the close.

findings.title: Intra-segment events are timestamped at the segment start: hold stats biased low, TPs credited after MaxHoldSec, pacing and cutoff gates too coarse
findings.detail: `_segment(S, wp[k], wp[k + 1], hs, p, tk, ...)` passes `tk = ti + wt[k]*60` (segment start). Every event in the segment uses that one t: `_close_side` (hold = t - START), `_open` (LASTADD = t), and `_adds_ok` (evaluated once at segment start). The time stop is only checked at the segment end. A TP reached after the MaxHoldSec limit but before the next waypoint is booked as a win, and its hold time is recorded as the segment start. NoAddAfterSec still allows adds for the whole segment that straddles the cutoff. AddMinSec is measured from the segment start instead of the fill time. With PathPoints=0 (the optimizer's robustness case), segments are 20 s long.
findings.failure_scenario: exp7_event_time.py: MaxHoldSec=25. A bull bar where TP = H at the 40 s waypoint. Sim: wins=1, time_stops=0, avg_hold_sec=20.0, +$5.00. The EA time-stops at 25 s near +$0.5.
findings.fix: Pass the segment end time too: `_segment(..., t0=tk, t1=ti + wt[k+1]*60)`. Stamp each event at `te = t0 + (cur - a) / (bnd - a) * (t1 - t0)`. Make the hold limit an event: if t_lim = START + hold_sec lies in [t0, t1], convert it to the price m = a + (t_lim - t0)/(t1 - t0)*(bnd - a) on the monotone leg and order it with the other events. Evaluate _adds_ok at te.

findings.title: Time-stop exits (and kill/daily/session/news/Friday market closes) get no slippage while the StopPips stop does
findings.detail: `_time_stops` calls `_close_side(S, sd, m, hs, p, t)` at the raw waypoint mid. The L1-anchored stop (ev 5) exits at `cur - slip` / `cur + slip`. Both are market closes in the EA (CloseAll). In HF configurations, time stops are a major exit type, so every one is under-costed by SlippagePts. The fit and the SlippagePts robustness case also miss this.
findings.failure_scenario: MaxHoldSec=60, SlippagePts=2: every time-stopped side books 0.2 pip x lots better than the stopped-side model. Over thousands of HF cycles this is a systematic optimistic bias of the same size as the stop slippage.
findings.fix: In `_time_stops`: `slip = p[31] * p[37]; fillm = (m - slip) if sd == 0 else (m + slip); S[STOPLOSS] += _close_side(S, sd, fillm, hs, p, t)`. Apply the same adverse shift in `_acct_guards` and in the session, news and Friday closes in run_core if those are meant to model market orders.

findings.title: Per-bar spread silently overrides SpreadPts/profile/rollover, and final equity is still marked with SpreadPts
findings.detail: With `use_sprd`, `spr_pts = sprd[i]`, so SpreadPts, UseSpreadProfile and RolloverSpreadMult have no effect at all. SpreadPts is still used for the final mark-to-market: `hs = p[32] * point * 0.5` at line 683. On an MT5 import, optimize_hf's robustness case `"spread x1.5": dict(SpreadPts=ACC["SpreadPts"] * 1.5)` is a no-op. The std account (SpreadPts=12) is also identical to std_raw minus commission. Open positions at the end are valued at a spread unrelated to the data.
findings.failure_scenario: Run optimize_hf robust mode on an mt5_import npz: the 'spread x1.5' row equals 'base' to the cent, so a cost-robustness test passes trivially.
findings.fix: Add a scale parameter, e.g. `spr_pts = sprd[i] * p[PI['SpreadScale']]`, or interpret SpreadPts as an additive markup when an array is present. Have optimize_hf scale it. For the final mark, keep the last bar's `hs` from the loop instead of recomputing it from p[32].

findings.title: Friday-close `continue` skips _build_path, so the random intrabar paths of every later bar depend on Friday settings
findings.detail: With PathPoints > 0, each bar consumes RNG draws in `_build_path`. The Friday-flatten branch `continue`s (line 597) before `_build_path` (line 671), so those bars consume nothing. Two configurations that differ only in CloseOnFriday or FridayCloseHour therefore get different Brownian paths for every bar after the first Friday evening. That breaks the common-random-numbers comparison the fixed PathSeed is supposed to provide.
findings.failure_scenario: Comparing CloseOnFriday=0 against CloseOnFriday=1 with PathPoints=3 attributes path noise to the Friday rule. Monday-onward TP/stop sequences differ even when no position was open on Friday.
findings.fix: Call `_build_path(wp, wt, o[i], h[i], l[i], c[i], npts)` (discarding the result) before the Friday `continue`. Alternatively, seed per bar, e.g. `np.random.seed(int(p[46]) * 1000003 + i)`, inside the path builder.

findings.title: grids_hit_max counts against MaxLayers, not the fitted ladder EFFML
findings.detail: `_open` does `if n >= p[6]: S[HITMAX] += 1`. When MaxBasketRiskPct or StopPips trims the ladder to EFFML < MaxLayers, a grid that uses every allowed layer is never counted. So `grids_hit_max` reads 0 for v7 configurations that hit their real cap.
findings.failure_scenario: StopPips=10, GridSpacingPts=30, MaxLayers=10: the fit gives EFFML=4. A grid that reaches 4 layers gives grids_hit_max=0.
findings.fix: Set `S[EFFML0]` / `S[EFFML1]` before calling `_open` in the entry block. In `_open`, compare `n >= min(p[6], S[EFFML0] if side == 0 else S[EFFML1])`.

verdicts.reason: `_acct_guards` returns at once when N0+N1==0 (bgrid_bt.py:714). The EA's V7AccountGuards (mq5:1306-1344) computes GridEquity() = balance + float on every tick, flat or not, and sets g_kill or g_dayHalt, which then blocks entries through sessOK (mq5:572). I reproduced this in review_verify/s1.py: $1000, 0.1-lot stretch BUY, StopPips=10, then 10 bars that each TP a fresh BUY. With DailyLossPct=0.5 or PeakKillPct=0.5 the sim gives daily_stops=0, killed=0, grids_opened=11, wins=10, balance 1040. With the early return removed (scratch copy fix1) it gives grids_opened=1, balance 990, and daily_stops=1 or killed=1, which matches the EA. All tests in test_bt.py still pass with the fix. One nuance: if a later grid stays open past a waypoint while equity is still under the limit, the latch fires late rather than never. A grid that TPs before the first waypoint can lift balance back above the limit, though, and then the breach is missed entirely. The kill flag feeds optimize_hf's score (ruin), so a missed latch also mis-scores configs. Small wording error in the finding: in EntryMode=1 both sides can be open at the same time (a later opposite signal), but usually only one is.
verdicts.corrected_fix: In bgrid_bt.py `_acct_guards`, delete the first two lines (`if S[N0] + S[N1] == 0:` / `return`). The rest stays as is: when flat, `_lin` gives A=B=0, so eq == S[BAL], and `_close_side` on an empty side returns 0.0 and changes nothing. The bar-open call (line 602) then catches a flat breach before the entry block, and the waypoint calls (line 679, gated on p[53]>0 or p[44]>0) catch it intrabar. The existing `if S[KILL] > 0 and flat: break` keeps working.

verdicts.reason: The kill and daily guards run only at waypoint ends (lines 678-679), and the close happens at wp[k+1]. Inside `_segment`, only x1 (EmergencyCloseDD) and x2 (stop-out) are solved as linear thresholds. Grid adds also keep filling inside the segment after equity has passed the limit. review_verify/s2.py, one 0.1-lot BUY and a bear bar 30 pips down: DailyLossPct=0.5 and PeakKillPct=0.5 both end at 970.00, against 995.00 for EmergencyCloseDD_Pct=0.5 or StopPips=5. With a 1-pip ladder (MaxLayers=10) DailyLossPct=0.5 ends at 745.00 with 9 adds, while EmergencyCloseDD ends at 995.00 with 2 adds. PathPoints=3 (the optimizer setting) shrinks the overshoot to 988.03 but does not remove it. The EA checks both guards on every tick, so it would exit near -$5.
verdicts.corrected_fix: In `_thresholds`, also return x3 (kill) = S[BAL] - S[PEAK]*(1 - p[53]/100) if p[53]>0 and S[KILL]==0, else 1e18. Return x4 (daily) = S[BAL] - S[DAYBAL]*(1 - p[44]/100) if p[44]>0 and S[DAYHALT]==0 and S[DAYBAL]>0, else 1e18. In `_segment`, add these to the immediate checks: `if fl_cur <= -x3:` close both sides at cur, add to STOPLOSS, set KILL=1, continue. `if fl_cur <= -x4:` close both sides, set DAYHALT=1, DAYSTOPS+=1, continue. In both direction branches, loop over the four thresholds (x2, x1, x3, x4) when solving ms = (-x - B)/A. Use event codes 3, 4, 6, 7, because 5 is already the side stop. Handle ev 6 and 7 as `_track`, close both sides at cur (no slip, like x1), set KILL or DAYHALT+DAYSTOPS, then `_track`. Add the same x3/x4 checks to `_jump` next to x1/x2. Between events A and B are constant and equity falls monotonically toward the threshold, so PEAK as of the current iteration is exact.

verdicts.reason: The BUY stop and SELL TP are tested only in the `down` branch, and the SELL stop and BUY TP only in the up branch. A segment with a==bnd counts as up (line 304), and equal waypoints are skipped (line 674). The inter-bar segment (line 588) is the first place a new bar's hs is applied, and it always runs, but on an up or flat move it cannot see a BUY stop that was crossed by a spread increase. review_verify/s3.py (StopPips=5, per-bar spread 0 then 140 pts, 0.1 lot): BUY on a bull bar is stopped at -7.00 (right), on a bear bar O->H->L->C at -5.00 (too late, at a better price), and on an up-only bar not at all. SELL is stopped at -7.00 in every case. The EA's V7GridExits fires on the first tick of the spike (-7.00). TPs crossed by a spread narrowing are missed the same way. Real-world impact is smaller than the toy cases, because most M1 bars have a down leg that catches it within the bar, and the optimizer's sessions end before the rollover spike. It hits every bar on MT5 per-bar-spread data. A scratch fix (fix3) gives -7.00 in all six cases and passes the tests.
verdicts.corrected_fix: In `_segment`, at the top of the event loop, after the x2/x1 immediate checks and before the direction branches, add direction-independent crossed-level checks, each ending in `continue`. (a) `if stop_d > 0 and S[N0] > 0 and cur <= S[FIRST0] - stop_d + hs:` `_track`, then `S[STOPLOSS] += _close_side(S, 0, cur - slip, hs, p, t)`, `S[SIDESTOPS] += 1`, continue. (b) `if stop_d > 0 and S[N1] > 0 and cur >= S[FIRST1] + stop_d - hs:` the same for side 1 at `cur + slip`. (c) `if S[N0] > 0 and cur - hs >= S[TP0] - 1e-9:` pnl = `_close_side(S, 0, cur, hs, p, t)`, TPPROFIT += pnl, WINS or LOSSES += 1, `_track`, continue. (d) `if S[N1] > 0 and cur + hs <= S[TP1] + 1e-9:` the same for side 1. Each must `continue` so that A, B and the thresholds are recomputed. This also puts stop before add on the same tick, as in the EA (V7GridExits runs before TryAddLayer). No change is needed for equal-price waypoint legs: hs only changes at bar boundaries, and the prev_c->o segment always runs.

verdicts.reason: Each add triggers at LAST-step, where LAST is the previous slipped fill, and fills at +slip. So fill_k = FIRST0 - (k-1)*(step - slip), and the realized loss per unit for layer k is dist_k + k*slip. `_fit_layers` charges dist_k + slip. The EA's TryAddLayer also anchors on the actual last fill (lastPx, mq5:718), so the same drift exists live. review_verify/s4.py (StopPips=10, 0.01 lots, budget $3.30): slip=5, step=20 fits 5 layers, the fit predicts $3.25, and the realized stop loss is $3.75, over budget. slip=2, step=20 realizes $3.30, exactly the budget, against a predicted $3.10. Only minor because SlippagePts is usually small relative to the spacing.
verdicts.corrected_fix: In `_fit_layers`: `dist = stop_d - (k - 1) * (step - slip)`. Use reachability as the cut-off: `if dist <= 2.0 * hs + slip: break`. The layer's trigger bid is fill_k - slip - 2hs, so it is reached before the stop only if dist > 2hs + slip. The simpler `dist <= 2.0*hs` is also safe, just slightly conservative. Keep `add = lot * p[27] * (dist + slip) + lot * p[28]`. Optional EA mirror in FitLayers: `double dist = stopD - (k - 1) * (step - slip); if(dist <= 2.0*halfSpread + slip) break;`, with RiskSlipPts standing in for add slippage.

verdicts.reason: The last Brownian leg uses tb=1.0, but the close is stamped 59/60. The last interior point, t2 + (1-t2)*npts/(npts+1), is later than 59/60 whenever t2 > 1 - (npts+1)/60. review_verify/s5.py over 200k bars: npts=3 gives 3.13% of bars with a backward step (worst -0.25 s), npts=5 gives 9.43% (-0.50 s), and npts=10 gives 25.2% (-0.73 s). This also makes the repo's own test flaky. test_random_path_stays_in_bar_and_is_seeded calls np.random.seed(3) from Python, and that does not seed numba's generator, so the path is effectively unseeded. Its monotonic-time assert failed in 3 of 30 runs of the unmodified `python3 test_bt.py`. Changing tb to 59/60 (scratch fix5) gives 0% backward steps for every npts. Impact on P/L is sub-second, so minor.
verdicts.corrected_fix: In `_build_path`, change `a, b, ta, tb = av2, av3, t2, 1.0` to `a, b, ta, tb = av2, av3, t2, 59.0 / 60.0` and keep `wt[k] = 59.0 / 60.0`. t2 <= 0.95 < 59/60, so all legs stay strictly ordered. Separately, make the test actually seeded by seeding numba's generator, e.g. through a tiny @njit helper `def _seed(s): np.random.seed(s)` called before `_build_path` in the test.

verdicts.reason: `_segment` gets tk = segment start (line 673), and every event inside it uses that time: `_close_side` hold, `_open` LASTADD, and `_adds_ok`, which is evaluated once at segment start (lines 305-306). The hold limit is checked only at waypoint ends (line 677). Re-running exp7 (MaxHoldSec=25, TP at the 40 s waypoint H) gives wins=1, time_stops=0, avg_hold_sec=20.0, +$5.00. Under the sim's own linear path the hold limit is reached at 25 s, at about +0.5 pip, so a TP after the limit is credited. L1 START is exact (bar open) while closes are stamped at segment start, so TP hold stats are biased low. AddMinSec and NoAddAfterSec get segment granularity: about 20 s with PathPoints=0, about 5 s with PathPoints=3. Waypoint granularity for the time stop itself is a documented approximation (test_v7_hold_in_seconds accepts 30-40 s). The in-segment ordering (TP before an already-expired hold limit) and the timestamps are real inconsistencies, though, and they bias short MaxHoldSec configs (30/60 s are in the search space) optimistically. Minor.
verdicts.corrected_fix: Pass both segment times, `_segment(S, wp[k], wp[k+1], hs, p, tk0, tk1, ...)` with tk0 = ti + wt[k]*60 and tk1 = ti + wt[k+1]*60, and also pass hold_sec. Inside, stamp each event at te = tk0 + (cur - a)/(bnd - a)*(tk1 - tk0) when bnd != a. Use te for `_close_side`, `_open` and `_try_add`, and re-evaluate `_adds_ok(S, side, p, te)` before each add event instead of once per segment. Add the hold limit as an event: for each open side, t_lim = START + hold_sec; if tk0 <= t_lim <= tk1, convert it to the price m_lim = a + (t_lim - tk0)/(tk1 - tk0)*(bnd - a), treat it as a candidate event (code 8) ordered with the others, and handle it like `_time_stops` (close that side at m_lim, TIMESTOPS += 1). Keep the waypoint `_time_stops` call for flat legs, which `_segment` skips.

verdicts.reason: The behaviour is as described: `_time_stops` closes at the raw mid, while the StopPips stop fills at cur -/+ slip. But the sim consistently uses SlippagePts as overshoot on price-triggered fills (grid adds and stops; see the module docstring: 'filled at the level (+ slippage). Real ticks can jump levels'). Other market orders that are not price-triggered get no slippage either, including the L1 market entry at bar open, which happens on every trade. Treating time-triggered market closes as slip-free is therefore a calibration choice consistent with that model, not a code bug. Whether time-stop market orders slip adversely on average is an empirical question. If the team decides that every market order should pay SlippagePts (as the doc's markout cost model charges 0.3 pip per trade), the change should cover L1 entries and all market closes uniformly, not only time stops.
verdicts.corrected_fix: Only if the cost model is changed so that market orders slip: in `_time_stops` use `fillm = m - p[31]*p[37] if sd == 0 else m + p[31]*p[37]` and pass it to `_close_side`. Do the same for the session, news, Friday and acct-guard closes, and the L1 open price (`px = o[i] + hs + slip` / `o[i] - hs - slip`).

verdicts.reason: When `sprd.shape[0] == n`, `spr_pts = sprd[i]` and SpreadPts, UseSpreadProfile and RolloverSpreadMult are all ignored. The final mark still uses `hs = p[32]*point*0.5` (line 683). review_verify/s8.py with a per-bar spread array: SpreadPts 2, 3 or 50, with UseSpreadProfile 0 or 1, all give the same final_balance 1006.9618, and only final_equity changes (979.74, 979.71, 978.30) through the end-of-run mark. Latent: the EURUSD npz from prep_data.py has no 'spread' field, so the reported robustness results are not affected.
verdicts.corrected_fix: Append a parameter `SpreadScale` (default 1.0) to PARAM_NAMES and EA_DEFAULTS, and use `spr_pts = sprd[i] * p[PI_SpreadScale]` (index 58) in the use_sprd branch. In optimize_hf robust, use `"spread x1.5": dict(SpreadPts=ACC["SpreadPts"]*1.5, SpreadScale=1.5)`. For the final mark, initialise `hs = p[32]*point*0.5` before the bar loop and delete the recomputation at line 683, so the mark uses the last processed bar's hs.

verdicts.reason: `_build_path` is the only RNG consumer. The Friday-flatten branch `continue`s (line 597) before `_build_path` (line 671), so Friday-evening bars consume no draws when CloseOnFriday=1, and every later path shifts. review_verify/s9.py (random walk, PathPoints=3, session 01:00-23:00 with close-at-end, so the Friday close only takes over the session close's role on the same bar at the same price): CloseOnFriday=0 gives balance 1020.3162 and 670 wins, CloseOnFriday=1/23h gives 1020.4609 and 671 wins. verdicts.reason: `_open` counts HITMAX only when n >= p[6] (MaxLayers). `_segment` stops adds at S[EFFML0] or S[EFFML1] (lines 323 and 350), so whenever the v7 fit trims the ladder (EFFML < MaxLayers), n never reaches p[6] and grids_hit_max reads 0 even for grids that exhausted their real cap. Reporting only (no P/L effect). It is not used by optimize_hf, but the v6 optimize.py prints it.
verdicts.corrected_fix: In run_core's entry block, set `S[EFFML0] = effml` before `_open(S, 0, ...)`, and `S[EFFML1] = effml` before `_open(S, 1, ...)`. With StopPips=0, effml == MaxLayers, so v6 behaviour is unchanged.

checked_ok: All 16 tests in research/test_bt.py pass.

_fit_layers per-layer loss with no slippage: dist = stop_d - (k-1)*step runs from the ask fill to the bid stop, so the spread is already included. Stop-exit slip and the round-turn commission (lot*CommPerLotRT) are included, and the arithmetic matches the EA's FitLayers. When StopPips=0 it returns MaxLayers, so v6 behaviour is unchanged. Layers with 0 < dist <= spread are unreachable but counting them is harmless.

L1-anchored stop levels in _segment are correct: BUY mid = FIRST0 - stop_d + hs (bid = L1 ask - stop), SELL mid = FIRST1 + stop_d - hs (ask = L1 bid + stop). FIRST0/FIRST1 are set only on the L1 open. Exits get adverse slippage: BUY at bid - slip, SELL at ask + slip. Verified at -10.20 for both sides with a 2-pip spread and 0.2-pip slip (exp5_stop_dirs.py).
_jump stops fill at the gap price with adverse slippage (SELL gap verified at -32.2). TP is checked before the stop; a stop is checked before adds, so no add happens past the stop.

_adds_ok matches the EA: NoAddAfterSec uses >= from the oldest fill, AddMinSec uses < from the newest fill. LASTADD includes L1, so the first add waits AddMinSec. ok0/ok1 are computed once per segment and cleared after a successful add when AddMinSec>0, and a blocked add disables adds for that segment. _jump re-evaluates _adds_ok after its closes. The EFFML cap is applied in both _segment and _jump.
The spread guard on adds (2*hs/point > MaxSpreadPts) is consistent with the open guard and the EA's SYMBOL_SPREAD > MaxSpreadPts.

The peak definition matches the EA: S[PEAK] is the running max of balance + EA float, updated by _track at every event and segment end; the EA uses GridEquity. The daily balance is BAL at the first bar of the server day and DAYHALT resets on a new day, both matching the EA. KILL and DAYHALT block opens. The early break once killed and flat is safe: equity is frozen, CAGR uses the full span, and report.py ffills the NaN daily tail.

stretch_signal has no lookahead. The raw signal at bar j uses c[j], o[j] and h/l[j-1]. It is shifted one row and consumed at o[i], so it uses bar i-1 (closed) and i-2, the same as the EA's CopyClose(...,1,...) with c[0], o[0], l[1], h[1]. The EWM alpha matches the EA: halflife 60 gives 1-0.5^(1/60), and span gives 2/(n+1). The trend term |c[j]-c[j-60]|/(sig1*sqrt60) and the reclaim conditions match both the EA and step0_markout. The pip scale cancels, so the cache key without pip is fine.

_time_stops uses START (oldest fill) with >= and a 1e-6 tolerance, and checks at the bar open and every waypoint with waypoint prices and times paired correctly. Minute-based MaxHoldMin still fires only at bar opens, because waypoints are < 60 s.
Deterministic _build_path times are 0/20/40/59 s and monotonic. Brownian points stay within [low, high].
Stats: the 31 STAT_NAMES align with the out[] indices. avg_hold_sec and max_hold_sec are the minute values x 60; HOLDSUM and MAXHOLD are kept in minutes.

Interaction with old features: no regressions found beyond the findings above. NewsPauseLayers gates only adds, not stops. A basket-stop HALT disables x1 but not the v7 stops. Stop-out still runs as an immediate check and a solved event. Friday flatten returns before v7 checks, as the EA does. Session close happens at the bar open and blocks opens. News pre-close is unchanged.

Numba forward references (_adds_ok, _acct_guards, _time_stops, _build_path defined after their callers) resolve correctly. The mt5_import spread is in points and is applied consistently as hs = spread*point/2.

findings.title: Sim never sets the kill latch or the daily stop while flat; the EA does
findings.detail: _acct_guards starts with `if S[N0] + S[N1] == 0: return`. A loss realised by an exit (StopPips stop inside a leg, time stop, session close) therefore never trips PeakKillPct or DailyLossPct, because the next check happens with the book flat. The EA's V7AccountGuards (mq5:1321, 1333) has no nOpen condition. It evaluates `eq = GridEquity()` (balance when flat) on the same tick as V7GridExits closes the grid, and latches or halts at once. In the sim the latch fires only if a later grid is still open at some waypoint. A grid that closes inside its first leg is never seen, so the sim keeps trading. The optimiser's score treats killed as ruin, so this undercounts ruin. Direction: sim optimistic.
findings.failure_scenario: Verified: BUY-only grid, Balance 1000, ZERO_COST, BaseLot 0.1, StopPips 30, PeakKillPct 2, a 40-pip drop, then bear bars where each new grid hits a 1-pip TP in its first leg. Sim result: killed=0, 31 grids, final $1000. The EA latches at equity <= $980 on the first tick past -2% and stays flat at $980. With DailyLossPct=1 the sim gives daily_stops=0. With a time stop realising the loss, the sim opens one extra grid before halting.

findings.title: Ladder-fit commission and slippage inputs are not tied to the simulator's cost model
findings.detail: The sim's _fit_layers uses the account cost model: `add = lot * p[27] * (dist + slip) + lot * p[28]`, with slip = SlippagePts and p[28] = CommPerLotRT (7.0 for std_raw). The EA uses separate inputs, `RiskSlipPts = 2.0` and `RiskCommPerLot = 0.0`, and nothing maps CommPerLotRT to RiskCommPerLot. For the frozen configs this gate is binding: it acts as an equity floor below which nothing opens. With the EA defaults the floor sits lower, so the EA keeps trading where the sim has stopped. The sim's robustness cases also move the gate: higher commission or slippage stops trading earlier and improves the final result. The EA's preset value would not move. Direction: the EA is more aggressive than the sim.
findings.failure_scenario: frozen is_rank1 (StopPips 27, MaxBasketRiskPct 3, 0.01 lot, std_raw). Sim layer-1 cost = $2.72 + $0.07 = $2.79, so fit=0 (no entries) below equity $93.00. EA cost with RiskCommPerLot=0 = $2.72, so fit=0 only below $90.67. Verified on the 2012-2016 run: sim equity stops changing after day 340 of 1393 at $92.984 and is idle for about 4 years. The reported -1.4%/yr is one year of trading. robust_is.csv shows 'commission $10' ending at $93.77 and 'slippage x2' at $93.0-93.6, both better than base ($92.98), because the floor rose.
findings.fix: Every preset must set RiskCommPerLot = CommPerLotRT and RiskSlipPts = SlippagePts (see M2). Change the EA side, since it is the side missing the information. Report the sim's idle fraction, the share of days with fit=0, next to CAGR. If robustness runs should vary costs without moving the gate, add separate fit-only params to the sim that mirror RiskSlipPts and RiskCommPerLot.

findings.title: Set-file writer drops every v7 input, so an HF preset runs the EA with all v7 modules off
findings.detail: EA_INPUTS lists only the v6.13 inputs, and build() keeps only known keys: `for k, v in cfg.items(): k = RENAME.get(k, k); if k in vals: vals[k] = v`. All v7 keys are silently discarded: MaxHoldSec, NoAddAfterSec, AddMinSec, StopPips, MaxBasketRiskPct, DailyLossPct, PeakKillPct, EntryMode, ZEntry, ZEmaBars, TrendTMax and LotMultiplier. The keys with different names or units are lost as well: EntryTFMin (minutes) vs EntryTF (enum), SessStartMin/SessEndMin (minutes) vs SessionStart/SessionEnd ("HH:MM"), SessCloseAtEnd vs CloseAtSessionEnd, SlippagePts vs RiskSlipPts, and CommPerLotRT vs RiskCommPerLot. frozen.json also stores optimiser meta-params ('Session', 'Ladder') that only optimize_hf.build() expands. The EA would load at EntryTF=M15 with no time stop, no L1 stop, no ladder fit, no daily or kill limits and no session, which is a completely different system.
findings.failure_scenario: Run make_sets.py on frozen.json (is_rank1: EntryMode 1, EntryTFMin 1, MaxHoldSec 600, StopPips 27, Session lateny_1923 ...). The .set contains only GridSpacingPts, TP_Pips, MaxLayers, News* and MaxSpreadPts. The EA then trades symmetric M15 grids with no exits other than TP.
findings.fix: Expand frozen params with optimize_hf.build() and merge ACC. Append the v7 inputs to EA_INPUTS in declaration order: ("LotMultiplier",0.0), ("EntryTF",15), ("EntryMode",0), ("ZEntry",1.5), ("ZEmaBars",90), ("TrendTMax",2.0), ("MaxHoldSec",0), ("NoAddAfterSec",0), ("AddMinSec",0), ("StopPips",0.0), ("BrokerSLBufferPips",2.0), ("MaxBasketRiskPct",0.0), ("RiskSlipPts",2.0), ("RiskCommPerLot",0.0), ("DailyLossPct",0.0), ("PeakKillPct",0.0), ("ResetKillLatch","false"), ("SessionStart",""), ("SessionEnd",""), ("CloseAtSessionEnd","false"). Add CloseAtSessionEnd and ResetKillLatch to BOOLS. Convert keys: EntryTF = int(EntryTFMin) (PERIOD_M1=1, M5=5, M15=15), SessionStart = f"{m//60:02d}:{m%60:02d}" for SessStartMin >= 0 (same for the end), CloseAtSessionEnd = SessCloseAtEnd, RiskSlipPts = SlippagePts, RiskCommPerLot = CommPerLotRT. Make unknown keys raise instead of being skipped.

findings.title: Sim charges no slippage on L1 opens or on any market exit except the StopPips stop
findings.detail: Layer 1 fills at `px = o[i] + hs` / `px = o[i] - hs` (lines 659/665) with no slip. The time stop (`_time_stops`: `_close_side(S, sd, m, hs, p, t)`), daily and kill closes (`_acct_guards`), session close (line 615), news pre-close and Friday close also fill at mid ± hs with no slip. Only adds (`_try_add`) and the L1 stop (ev 5 / _jump) pay SlippagePts. In the EA all of these are market orders (MarketSend / CloseAll) and slip live; only the TP is a resting broker order. The frozen HF configs use MaxLayers=1 and exit mostly by TP or time stop, so SlippagePts barely reaches them, and the 'slippage x2' robustness case is close to a no-op. Direction: sim optimistic by up to 2 x SlippagePts per cycle. At std_raw that is 0.4 pip, compared with a measured gross edge of 0.15-0.5 pip.
findings.failure_scenario: Verified: 1-layer BUY grid closed by MaxHoldSec=30 on a flat tape. final_balance is 1000.0 for SlippagePts = 0, 2 and 20 alike.
findings.fix: Sim: `slip = p[31] * point`. L1: `px = o[i] + hs + slip` (BUY) / `o[i] - hs - slip` (SELL). Keep the TP on the requested price as the EA does (OpenLayer1 uses tick.ask): `S[TP0] = round((o[i] + hs + tpd) / point) * point`. FIRST0/FIRST1 = px (the EA anchors the stop to the actual fill). In _time_stops, _acct_guards, the session, news and Friday closes, pass `m - slip` for side 0 and `m + slip` for side 1 to _close_side, as ev 5 already does.

findings.title: MaxHoldSec fires only at the end of a waypoint leg; TPs and adds in the overshoot are credited
findings.detail: The intrabar loop runs `_segment(... wp[k] -> wp[k+1] ...)` and only afterwards `_time_stops(S, wp[k + 1], hs, p, ti + wt[k + 1] * 60.0, hold_sec)`. A deadline that falls inside a leg is applied at the leg's end, at the leg-end price (often the bar's H or L when PathPoints=0). Any TP or add in between still happens. The EA checks `tk.time_msc - oldestMs >= MaxHoldSec*1000` on every tick (mq5:1295) and closes at the deadline. The overshoot is up to 20 s with PathPoints=0 and up to about 13 s with PathPoints=3 (leg lengths are random). That is large next to the 30/60/120 s values the optimiser searches. Direction: sim optimistic, since each basket gets extra time to reach TP.
findings.failure_scenario: Verified: MaxHoldSec=30, TP 2 pips, bull bar O 1.1000 -> L 1.0995 (20 s) -> H 1.1003 (40 s). Sim: wins=1, +$2.00 (TP at about 37.5 s). EA: time stop at 30 s at about 1.0999, -$1.00.
findings.fix: Split the leg at the deadline. For each open side compute `dl = START + hold_sec`. If `tk < dl <= tk1` (tk1 = ti + wt[k+1]*60), set `f = (dl - tk) / (tk1 - tk)` and `mx = wp[k] + f * (wp[k+1] - wp[k])`. Then run `_segment(S, wp[k], mx, ...)`, `_time_stops(S, mx, hs, p, dl, hold_sec)`, and `_segment(S, mx, wp[k+1], ...)`. Apply the same split to the inter-bar segment prev_c -> o[i].

findings.title: Events inside a leg are stamped with the leg-start time, which skews NoAddAfterSec and AddMinSec
findings.detail: _segment receives one time `t` (the leg start) and uses it for `ok0 = allow0 and _adds_ok(S, 0, p, t)` (evaluated once per leg) and for `_open(S, side, fill, lot, p, t)` (LASTADD). Consequences: (a) NoAddAfterSec still allows adds up to one leg after the cutoff, whereas the EA blocks at `tick.time_msc - oldestMs >= NoAddAfterSec*1000`. (b) An add made late in a leg is stamped at the leg start, so the next add is allowed sooner than in the EA, which measures from the newest position's POSITION_TIME_MSC. (c) With AddMinSec > 0 the sim allows at most one add per leg even when AddMinSec is shorter than the leg. (d) TP closes record hold time from the leg start (max_hold_sec=20 where the true time is about 37 s). Direction: mixed; usually the sim is more permissive on adds.
findings.failure_scenario: AddMinSec=15, PathPoints=0. An add at about 35 s (leg 20-40 s) is stamped 20 s. The next leg starts at 40 s, 40-20 >= 15, so a second add at about 41 s is allowed. The EA blocks until 50 s.
findings.fix: Pass the leg end time into _segment. Stamp each event at `te = t0 + (t1 - t0) * (cur - a) / (bnd - a)`, use te in _open and _close_side, and re-evaluate `_adds_ok(S, side, p, te)` per add event instead of once per leg. If AddMinSec is still pending, add `LASTADD + AddMinSec` as a time event.

findings.title: Daily-loss and kill thresholds are checked only at waypoints, not at the exact crossing
findings.detail: `if p[53] > 0 or p[44] > 0: _acct_guards(S, wp[k + 1], ...)` runs after the whole leg. The EA checks every tick and closes at the first tick past the threshold. In the sim a threshold crossed mid-leg is acted on at the leg-end price. If a StopPips or time-stop exit happens in that leg first, the crossing is missed altogether (and C1 then skips it while flat). EmergencyCloseDD and stop-out are already solved exactly (x1/x2) in _segment, but these two are not. Direction: sim pessimistic on loss size; it also pays an extra round trip when the halt comes one grid late.
findings.failure_scenario: Verified: DailyLossPct=1% ($10) and StopPips=30 on a 0.1-lot BUY with a 40-pip drop. The sim realises -$30 at the stop and halts only on the next grid. The EA halts at -$10 float.
findings.fix: In _segment, add the two thresholds as linear-crossing events next to x1 and x2: `x3 = S[BAL] - S[DAYBAL]*(1 - p[44]/100)` (float loss that trips the daily stop, when DAYHALT==0) and `x4 = S[BAL] - S[PEAK]*(1 - p[53]/100)` (when KILL==0). Solve `ms = (-x - B)/A` as done for x1/x2. At the crossing, close both sides and set DAYHALT/DAYSTOPS or KILL, matching the EA's per-tick check.

findings.title: EA forgets a daily stop on any re-init; the equity peak is saved only in OnDeinit
findings.detail: OnInit always runs `g_dayStart = 0; g_dayHalt = false;`, so the first tick after any re-init sets `g_dayBal = AccountInfoDouble(ACCOUNT_BALANCE)` and clears a daily stop that has already fired. Re-inits include a terminal restart, an input edit or a chart-period change. The sim keeps DAYBAL/DAYHALT for the whole server day. `GlobalVariableSet(GvName("eqpeak"), g_eqPeak)` is written only in OnDeinit (line 379), so after a crash the persisted peak is stale and the kill threshold effectively loosens. Direction: EA more aggressive than the sim.
findings.failure_scenario: The daily stop fires at -5% at 10:00. The user changes an input or the terminal restarts at 10:05. The EA re-bases the day to the post-loss balance and resumes trading the same day; the sim would stay flat until midnight.
findings.fix: Persist dayStart, dayBal and dayHalt as GlobalVariables (GvName("dayStart"/"dayBal"/"dayHalt")) when they change. In OnInit restore them if the stored dayStart equals today's server midnight. Write eqpeak whenever g_eqPeak rises (throttled, e.g. at most once a minute), not only in OnDeinit.

findings.title: EA guard equity uses the account-wide balance; sim equity is EA-only
findings.detail: `GridEquity()` returns `AccountInfoDouble(ACCOUNT_BALANCE) + FloatPnL(MagicBuy) + FloatPnL(MagicSell)`. The kill peak, the daily base and the ladder-fit budget therefore move with deposits, withdrawals and other EAs' or manual trades' realised P/L on the same account. The sim's BAL is the EA's own P/L only. The float is EA-scoped but the balance is not, so the stated 'grid-scoped' immunity does not hold for these guards.
findings.failure_scenario: PeakKillPct=25 on an account at its peak of $120. The user withdraws $40, and the EA latches the kill on the next tick with no trading loss. Another EA's losing day trips this EA's DailyLossPct.
findings.fix: Use an EA-scoped balance: a persisted start balance plus the sum of DEAL_PROFIT, DEAL_SWAP and DEAL_COMMISSION of this EA's magics (HistorySelect), cached and updated when a grid closes. Alternatively, state 'dedicated account only' and refuse to run (or warn) when foreign positions or balance operations are detected.

findings.title: Lot rounding: sim rounds half to even, EA rounds half away from zero
findings.detail: The sim uses `lot = np.round(lot / step) * step` (banker's rounding). The EA uses `NormalizeDouble(MathRound(lot / step) * step, 2)`; MathRound rounds half away from zero. Exact halves occur with common LotMultiplier and LotIncrement choices, and there the sim uses one step less. That changes the sim's risk and its _fit_layers ladder relative to the EA. Direction: sim lots smaller, so the sim is optimistic on risk.
findings.failure_scenario: Each pair gives sim vs EA lots: BaseLot 0.03, LotMultiplier 1.5, layer FlatLayers+1: 0.045 -> sim 0.04, EA 0.05. BaseLot 0.01 x 2.5 -> 0.02 vs 0.03. BaseLot 0.05 x 1.3 -> 0.06 vs 0.07. BaseLot 0.1 x 1.05 -> 0.10 vs 0.11. Additive 0.01 + 0.015 -> 0.02 vs 0.03. There are 25 such cases in a grid over BaseLot 0.01-0.3 and mult 1.05-3.0. The optimiser's current space (0.01 steps, multiplier 0) avoids them.
findings.fix: Sim: `lot = np.floor(lot / step + 0.5) * step` (lots are positive), which matches MathRound. The existing geometric-ladder test still passes.

findings.title: Fitted ladder depth is not persisted; a restart refits it from current equity
findings.detail: `g_effMaxLayers[k] = (cnt > 0) ? (int)MathMax(cnt, FitLayers(GridEquity())) : MaxLayers;`. The sim fixes EFFML when layer 1 opens and keeps it for the basket's life. After a restart the EA refits from today's equity. That can be deeper than the original fit (for example, the other side banked a profit in the meantime) or shallower. If SYMBOL_TRADE_TICK_VALUE is not ready at OnInit, FitLayers returns 0 and the grid is frozen at its current count.
findings.failure_scenario: The BUY grid opened with fit=2. The SELL grid then wins, raising equity, and the terminal restarts. The refit returns 3 and the EA adds a third layer the sim would never add.
findings.fix: At OpenLayer1 success, also `GlobalVariableSet(GvName(k==0?"effBuy":"effSell"), fit)`. In OnInit, restore that value when positions exist, and fall back to the refit only if it is missing.

findings.title: EA stop anchor and hold clock follow the oldest live position, not layer 1
findings.detail: GridTimes returns the oldest live position's POSITION_TIME_MSC and price as `firstPx`, and StopPrice, BrokerSL, EnsureSL, MaxHoldSec and NoAddAfterSec all use it. The sim uses FIRST*/START* for the whole life of the basket. If layer 1 closes alone, the anchor drifts to layer 2's fill, one spacing worse, and the age clock restarts. This can happen when an add's SetTP fails (adds are sent with tp=0) and layer 1 reaches the new TP before HealTP runs a minute later.
findings.failure_scenario: BUY layer 2 has no TP after a failed SetTP, and layer 1 hits TP. The remaining basket's stop moves GridSpacingPts lower and MaxHoldSec restarts from layer 2's time. The sim would have closed the whole basket at TP.
findings.fix: Anchor the stop to the basket extreme instead: the max open price for BUY or the min for SELL, which is layer 1's fill. Measure age from a persisted layer-1 time in ms, recorded at OpenLayer1 from POSITION_TIME_MSC, or from g_buyGridStart/g_sellGridStart stored in ms.

verdicts.reason: _acct_guards (bgrid_bt.py:714) returns at once when the book is flat, and both call sites (bar open, line 602; waypoints, line 679) can only run after an exit has already flattened the side. The EA's V7AccountGuards (mq5:1306-1344) has no nOpen condition. It runs on every tick right after V7GridExits, with eq = GridEquity(), which is the balance when flat, so it latches or halts at once. Reproduced in scratchpad/review_verify/c1.py: a BUY-only 0.1-lot grid (Balance 1000, zero cost, StopPips 30) takes a 40-pip drop, then a series of bars where each new grid hits a 1-pip TP in its first leg. The original sim gives PeakKillPct=2 -> killed=0, 41 grids, final $1010; DailyLossPct=1 -> daily_stops=0; with MaxHoldSec=30 also killed=0. With the early return deleted, all three latch or halt after the stop at $970 (1 or 2 grids). All 16 tests in test_bt.py still pass with the patch. The optimiser scores killed as ruin, so it undercounts ruin.
verdicts.corrected_fix: In bgrid_bt.py _acct_guards, delete the two lines `if S[N0] + S[N1] == 0:\n        return`. With the book flat, eq = S[BAL] + _lin(...) = S[BAL], which mirrors GridEquity(). _close_side already returns 0.0 for an empty side, so the flatten loops are harmless. Keep the bar-open call (line 602) before the open block so a flat latch or halt blocks that bar's opens; the open block already checks S[KILL]==0 and S[DAYHALT]==0.

verdicts.reason: The sim's _fit_layers charges `lot*cs*(dist+slip) + lot*p[28]` from the account model; std_raw is SlippagePts=2, CommPerLotRT=7 (optimize_hf.py:40). The EA's FitLayers uses separate inputs RiskSlipPts=2.0 and RiskCommPerLot=0.0, and nothing in the repo maps CommPerLotRT to RiskCommPerLot. For is_rank1 (0.01 lot, StopPips 27, budget 3%), the sim's layer-1 cost is 1000*(0.0027+0.00002)+0.07 = $2.79, so it stops opening below $93.00. The EA's cost is $2.72, so it stops only below $90.67. Reproduced on the real data with optimize_hf.evaluate(build(is_rank1), IS, daily=True): equity last changes at day index 340 of 1393, at $92.984, with 344 grids. So 75% of the in-sample period is idle and the -1.4%/yr is about one year of trading. 'slippage x2' is also idle from day 340 (final $93.024). This explains why robust_is.csv shows identical results for every seed and for the OHLC path, and why 'commission $10' ends higher than base. The EA cannot read the commission itself, so the preset has to carry it.
verdicts.corrected_fix: Bridge (make_sets / the v7 preset writer, see M2): always emit RiskCommPerLot = CommPerLotRT and RiskSlipPts = SlippagePts from the account model (std_raw -> RiskCommPerLot=7, RiskSlipPts=2). Optionally have OnInit print the fit-floor equity (the smallest equity with FitLayers>=1) so a mismatch is visible. Sim/report: report the idle fraction next to CAGR (days with no grid and fit=0, or the share of the period after equity last changes). If the robustness cost cases should stress P/L without moving the gate, add fit-only params (e.g. FitSlipPts, FitCommPerLot, defaulting to SlippagePts and CommPerLotRT) that mirror the EA's RiskSlipPts and RiskCommPerLot.

verdicts.reason: These fills carry no slippage: L1 at `o[i] ± hs` (lines 659/665), _time_stops, _acct_guards, the session close (615), the news pre-close (623) and the Friday close (593). Only _try_add and the StopPips exit (ev 5 and _jump) apply p[31]. Reproduced: a 1-layer BUY time-stopped at 30 s on a flat tape gives final_balance 1000.0 for SlippagePts 0, 2 and 20 alike. In the EA, all of these are MarketSend/CloseAll market orders. One nuance: against the MT5 real-tick tester without Random delay this is parity, because market orders fill at the tick. The defect is against live execution and against the research's own cost model: HF_GRID_RESEARCH.md calls the std_raw results 'raw-ECN costs (... + slippage)' and says 'slippage x2' leaves the conclusion unchanged. For MaxLayers=1 TP/time-stop cycles that case is effectively a no-op; it only moves the fit gate (see M1).
verdicts.corrected_fix: `slip = p[31]*point`. L1 opens: BUY `px = o[i] + hs + slip`, SELL `px = o[i] - hs - slip`. _open sets FIRST0/FIRST1 = px, matching the EA's stop anchored on the actual fill. Compute the TP from the requested price as OpenLayer1 does: `S[TP0] = round((o[i]+hs+tpd)/point)*point`, `S[TP1] = round((o[i]-hs-tpd)/point)*point`. For every market exit (_time_stops, _acct_guards, session close, news pre-close, Friday close, and _loss_close for the basket stop and stop-out), pass `m - slip` for side 0 and `m + slip` for side 1 to _close_side, as ev 5 already does. TP closes (ev 2 and the _jump TP) stay unslipped.

verdicts.reason: The hold limit is checked only after each full leg (`_time_stops(S, wp[k+1], ..., ti + wt[k+1]*60)`), but TPs, adds and stops inside the leg are solved continuously. A deadline that falls inside a leg is therefore applied at the leg-end price, which with PathPoints=0 is the bar's H or L, and any TP in between is credited. Reproduced: MaxHoldSec=30, TP 2 pips, bull bar O 1.1000/L 1.0995/H 1.1003. The original sim gives wins=1, +$2.00, max_hold_sec=20 (the TP is stamped at the leg start). The same symptom drives the doc's '+245%' artifact (a 30 s stop exiting on the bar's high or low). PathPoints=0 does not emulate MT5 OHLC ticks exactly anyway, since adds and TPs are filled at levels along the legs, so the time stop should be solved on the same continuous path. Prototype fix (scratchpad bt_m4.py): the same bar gives time_stops=1 at 30 s and -$1.00. All 16 tests pass, including test_v7_hold_in_seconds.

_segment takes a single time t (the leg start). It evaluates `_adds_ok` once per leg and stamps _open (LASTADD, and START for adds) and _close_side (the hold stats) with t. So NoAddAfterSec can admit adds up to one leg past the cutoff, and a late-in-leg add is stamped early, which lets the next leg's add through sooner than the EA's `tick.time_msc - newestMs` check. With AddMinSec > 0, line 387 caps adds at one per leg even when AddMinSec is shorter than the leg (conservative). The M4 reproduction also shows the TP close recorded with max_hold_sec=20 when the true time is about 37.5 s. A falling bar with AddMinSec=15 gave 2 adds against 40 unpaced, which shows the one-per-leg cap. The direction is mixed, as the finding says.
verdicts.corrected_fix: Give _segment(t0, t1) and stamp each event at `te = t0 + (t1 - t0) * (cur - a) / (bnd - a)` (te = t0 when bnd == a). Pass te to _open, _close_side, _loss_close and _try_add. Re-evaluate `_adds_ok(S, side, p, te)` at each candidate add event instead of once per leg. Drop the 'one add per leg' latch and instead add the time events LASTADD+AddMinSec and START+NoAddAfterSec as split points, the same way as the M4 deadline split.

verdicts.reason: DailyLossPct and PeakKillPct are evaluated only at waypoints (line 678) and at the bar open, while EmergencyCloseDD and stop-out are solved exactly in _segment (x1/x2). The EA checks every tick, so with DailyLossPct=1% on $1000 and a 0.1-lot BUY falling 40 pips it halts at about -$10 float. In the sim the StopPips stop (-$30) fires first inside the leg. Because of C1 the halt is then missed altogether; with C1 fixed it would happen at -$30. The formulas are correct: eq - DAYBAL <= -pct*DAYBAL  <=>  fl <= -(BAL - DAYBAL*(1-pct)), and similarly for the peak. Along a monotone leg the equity peak is at the leg start, so using S[PEAK] at the leg start is exact.
verdicts.corrected_fix: In _thresholds or _segment, add `x3 = S[BAL] - S[DAYBAL]*(1 - p[44]/100)` when p[44]>0, S[DAYHALT]==0 and S[DAYBAL]>0, and `x4 = S[BAL] - S[PEAK]*(1 - p[53]/100)` when p[53]>0 and S[KILL]==0. Include them in the immediate check `fl_cur <= -x` and in the crossing solve `ms = (-x - B)/A`, as for x1/x2, with new event codes. On the event, call _track, close both sides into STOPLOSS (with the M3 slip), then set DAYHALT=1, DAYSTOPS+=1 or KILL=1. Do not call _loss_close, which sets HALT and BASKETS. Keep the waypoint _acct_guards as a backstop.

verdicts.reason: OnInit unconditionally runs `g_dayStart = 0; g_dayHalt = false;` (mq5:306-307). The first tick then re-bases g_dayBal to the post-loss balance and clears a daily stop that has already fired. This happens on every re-init (input edit, chart change, terminal restart). The sim keeps DAYBAL and DAYHALT for the whole server day. eqpeak is written only in OnDeinit (line 379). In addition, MT5 writes GlobalVariables to disk only at a normal terminal shutdown or on GlobalVariablesFlush(), so after a crash even the kill flag set at line 1324 can be lost.
verdicts.corrected_fix: Persist the daily state whenever it changes: GlobalVariableSet(GvName("dayStart"), (double)(long)g_dayStart), GvName("dayBal"), GvName("dayHalt"). In OnInit, compute today's server midnight. If GvName("dayStart") equals it, restore g_dayStart, g_dayBal and g_dayHalt instead of zeroing them. Write GvName("eqpeak") whenever g_eqPeak rises, throttled (e.g. at most once per 60 s, and always before a kill check). Call GlobalVariablesFlush() after setting kill, dayHalt and eqpeak so they survive a crash.

verdicts.reason: GridEquity() = AccountInfoDouble(ACCOUNT_BALANCE) + FloatPnL(MagicBuy) + FloatPnL(MagicSell) (mq5:1202-1205). It drives g_eqPeak, the daily base g_dayBal and FitLayers. Deposits, withdrawals, credit and other strategies' realised P/L therefore move all three, while the sim's BAL is the EA's P/L only. A withdrawal of $40 from a $120 peak with PeakKillPct=25 gives eq 80 <= 90, a persisted kill latch with no trading loss. A deposit permanently raises g_eqPeak, so withdrawing it later trips the kill. The code does not claim grid-scoped immunity for the v7 guards (that comment is about gridDD), but the divergence from the sim and the operational hazard are real. Minor.
verdicts.corrected_fix: Neutralise balance operations while keeping the account-level semantics. Each tick (or throttled), HistorySelect from the last-seen time. For every deal with DEAL_TYPE_BALANCE, DEAL_TYPE_CREDIT, DEAL_TYPE_BONUS or DEAL_TYPE_CHARGE, shift g_eqPeak and g_dayBal by its DEAL_PROFIT. Persist the last-seen deal time. Alternatively, use an EA-scoped balance (a persisted start balance plus the sum of DEAL_PROFIT+DEAL_SWAP+DEAL_COMMISSION over deals with this EA's magics). At minimum, warn in OnInit and on detection when foreign positions or balance operations exist, and document 'dedicated account only'.

verdicts.reason: In IEEE doubles, lot/step can be an exact .5 (for example 0.03*1.5/0.01 == 4.5 exactly). numba's np.round rounds half to even, and MQL5's MathRound rounds half away from zero (C round). Reproduced: 0.03x1.5 -> sim 0.04 / EA 0.05; 0.01x2.5 -> 0.02/0.03; 0.05x1.3 -> 0.06/0.07; 0.1x1.05 -> 0.10/0.11; additive 0.01+0.015 -> 0.02/0.03. A sweep over BaseLot 0.01-0.30, mult 1.05-3.00 and layers 2-7 gives 56 mismatches. The proposed fix gives 0.05 and 0.03, keeps test_geometric_ladder_from_001 ([0.01,0.02,0.02,0.03,0.05,0.08]) and passes all 16 tests. The current optimiser space (LotMultiplier=0, 0.01 increments) does not produce exact halves.
verdicts.corrected_fix: bgrid_bt.py _lot_size: replace `lot = np.round(lot / step) * step` with `lot = np.floor(lot / step + 0.5) * step` (lots are positive, so this equals MathRound).

verdicts.reason: OnInit refits the per-side ladder depth from current equity with `(int)MathMax(cnt, FitLayers(GridEquity()))` (mq5:311). The sim fixes EFFML when layer 1 opens and keeps it for the basket's life. After a restart the EA can therefore allow more layers (equity rose, e.g. the other side banked a win) or fewer than the original fit. If SYMBOL_TRADE_TICK_VALUE is still 0 at OnInit, FitLayers returns 0 and MathMax freezes the grid at its current count. This only happens on a restart. Minor.
verdicts.corrected_fix: After a successful OpenLayer1, also `GlobalVariableSet(GvName(k==0?"effBuy":"effSell"), fit); GlobalVariablesFlush();`. In OnInit, when cnt > 0 and that GV exists, use g_effMaxLayers[k] = (int)MathMax(cnt, GlobalVariableGet(...)). Fall back to the refit only when it is missing. When FitLayers returns 0 because the tick value is not ready, defer the refit to the first tick instead of freezing at cnt. Delete the GV when the side goes flat.

verdicts.reason: Confirmed with a corrected fix. GridTimes takes firstPx and oldestMs from the oldest live position, and StopPrice, BrokerSL, EnsureSL, MaxHoldSec and NoAddAfterSec all use them. When layer 1 closes without the rest, the anchor slides one spacing (EnsureSL then moves every broker SL with it) and the age clock restarts from layer 2. The stated SetTP-failure path is real but mild, because the price is at the TP, far from the stop, and HealTP closes the rest within a minute. The stronger path is a partial CloseAll failure on the basket stop or time stop in V7GridExits. The CloseAll result is ignored. On the next tick the remaining layers have a further stop and a younger age, so the triggered exit is never completed: this is the half-closed basket that the v6.13 g_haltFlatten fix prevents for the emergency stop. The finding's proposed stop fix does not work: once layer 1 is gone, the max open price of the remaining BUY positions is layer 2's fill, the same as the oldest. It only matters for MaxLayers > 1.
verdicts.corrected_fix: (1) Store a per-side layer-1 anchor at OpenLayer1 success. Select the new position and set g_l1Px[k] = POSITION_PRICE_OPEN and g_l1Ms[k] = POSITION_TIME_MSC. Persist both via GlobalVariables (GvName("l1PxBuy"/"l1MsBuy"/...)) and clear them when PosCount(magic)==0. Use them, rather than GridTimes' oldest position, in StopPrice, BrokerSL, EnsureSL, the MaxHoldSec and NoAddAfterSec checks, and TTryAddLayer's SL. In OnInit, restore them from the GVs when positions exist, or fall back to the oldest position. (2) Add a per-side exit latch `bool g_exitPending[2]`, set when V7GridExits fires a basket stop or time stop. Each tick, if it is set and PosCount(magic)>0, call CloseAll(magic) and skip that side's adds and opens. Clear it once the side is flat.

checked_ok: EntryTF timing: the EA's new-bar check (iTime(EntryTF,0) != g_lastBar on the first tick) matches the sim's `ti // tf_sec != last_m15` at the bar open. Gates are evaluated once per bar with no retry inside the bar. The order is the same in both: exits, then guards, then adds, then opens, so a time-stopped side can reopen on the same bar-open tick. Early returns in the EA (guards, halt flatten, Friday) never cause a mid-bar open, because the blocking gate is still false when the open is finally evaluated.

STRETCH formula matches line by line. sigma uses a = 1 - 0.5^(1/60) (pandas halflife=60). The EMA uses alpha = 2/(N+1), adjust=False. z = (c - EMA)/pip/(sig1*sqrt15). The trend veto |c0 - c60|/(sig1*sqrt60) >= TrendTMax equals rolling(60).sum(). The reclaim tests c>o && c>prev low (BUY) and c<o && c<prev high (SELL). Series indexing (o[0], l[1], h[1] with ArraySetAsSeries) is correct. The signal comes from the last closed M1 bar and acts on the next bar's open, the same as the sim's shift(1). Seeding differences over 1200 bars are about 1e-6.
MaxHoldSec age: both measure from the layer-1 fill time (oldest position vs START), use >=, and close the whole side; only the evaluation timing differs (M4).
NoAddAfterSec is measured from layer 1 and AddMinSec from the newest position including layer 1 in both; the semantics match apart from leg stamping (N1).

StopPips level and side: BUY triggers on bid <= L1 ask fill - StopPips and SELL on ask >= L1 bid fill + StopPips, identical in _segment (FIRST0 - stop_d + hs, FIRST1 + stop_d - hs), _jump and EA StopPrice. It is checked before adds on the same path, and the sim stop fill includes slippage.

The broker SL sits BrokerSLBufferPips beyond the virtual stop on the same price side (bid for BUY, ask for SELL), so it never fires first on continuous ticks. SetTP now keeps the SL, and EnsureSL re-anchors it to the real layer-1 fill. No sim counterpart is needed.

FitLayers matches _fit_layers exactly: dist = stopD - (k-1)*step, plus slip, plus lot x round-trip commission, against a budget of % of (balance + EA float) taken before layer 1 for both sides; it stops at the first layer that does not fit, and fit < 1 blocks both opens. Tick value tv/ts = 100000 = ContractSize for EURUSD on a USD (or USC cent) account. Only the input values differ (M1).
Effective max layers is set only when layer 1 opens successfully, and adds are gated by count < min(eff, MaxLayers) in the EA vs N < EFFML in the sim. It is not reset by later adds in either.

MaxSpreadPts on adds: both use 'spread > MaxSpreadPts blocks'. A blocked add does not consume the level, and the add happens later at the then-current (deeper) price. The sim is bar-resolution because spread is constant per bar.

DailyLossPct base is the balance at the first tick or bar of the server day (swap stays in the float in both). Equity is balance + EA float including swap and excluding exit commission. The threshold formula and the halt until the next server day are identical, and the kill is checked before the daily limit in both.

PeakKillPct peak is the running max of balance + float from the start balance, including float spikes at bar extremes. The latch is permanent in both, and the EA persists the kill flag the moment it fires.

Session window: minutes after server midnight, [start, end) with midnight wrap, and start == end means off, in both. New grids are gated only by the session; CloseAtSessionEnd flattens at the first tick or bar at or after SessionEnd. Adds are not session-gated in either.
LotMultiplier formula BaseLot*mult^(layer-FlatLayers) and the rounding order (round to step, then VolMin clamp) match; only half-way rounding differs (N5).

The layer-1 TP is set from the requested price in the EA and from the fill in the sim, which is identical while the sim's layer-1 fill has no slippage. Add trigger levels match: ask <= last - step for BUY, bid >= last + step for SELL.
